papers.title: An equivariant index theorem for the Heisenberg calculus
papers.abstract: We derive a local fixed-point formula for the equivariant index of Heisenberg elliptic operators on closed contact manifolds equipped with an action of a compact Lie group preserving the contact form. The formula expresses the character of the equivariant index in terms of a cyclic-cohomological character of the noncommutative Heisenberg principal symbol. The main new ingredient is the construction of traces, one on each fixed-point set, defined by integration over twisted conjugacy classes in the Heisenberg group. The proof proceeds by a K-theoretic reduction to the equivariant index theorem of our paper "Toeplitz operators on contact manifolds and equivariant K-homology".

papers.title: An internal approach to symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories
papers.abstract: We propose a definition of symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories as special left double $(\infty,n)$-fibrations over the category of finite pointed sets. The definition makes sense in a general model of $(\infty,n)$-categories, under a mild condition on its discrete objects, and when the model is left proper and combinatorial we construct model structures whose fibrant objects are exactly these fibrations. For $n=1$ we show that the definition recovers Lurie's symmetric monoidal $(\infty,1)$-categories: the homotopy theory of special left double $(\infty,1)$-fibrations is equivalent to that of special coCartesian fibrations over the category of finite pointed sets. The equivalence is realized by an explicit Quillen equivalence, and two constructions, the staircase and coCartesian strings, translate between the two descriptions.

papers.title: The Borel Topos
papers.abstract: We construct a topos for Borel mathematics: statements which are true in Borel mathemaics correspond in a precise way to statements which are true in the internal logic of this topos. We investigate several other properties of this topos, including proving that it satisfies a Borel analogue of the Church-Turing thesis: the statement that every function on a standard Borel space is Borel. We also show that an earlier construction of a similar "Borel topos" by van Osdol does not suit these purposes because of an error in that paper.

papers.title: A Barsotti-Weil isomorphism for Taelman units
papers.abstract: The positive-characteristic analogue of motivic cohomology with coefficients in an Anderson A-motive M over a function field of transcendence degree one was introduced in an earlier work of the author. In this paper, we prove that, when M arises as the dual of the A-motive of an Anderson module E that is abelian, uniformizable, and has everywhere good reduction, the corresponding A-motivic cohomology coincides with the module of Taelman units of E, up to a twist by the module of K\"ahler differentials of A. To this end, we recast the theory of Anderson generating functions in the spirit of earlier work of Maurischat and the author on special functions.

papers.title: Characterizing $2$-slices over finite groups
papers.abstract: For a finite group $G$, we characterize the $2$-slices of $G$-spectra in the regular slice filtration in terms of their homotopy Mackey functors and $k$-invariant. We explicitly compute this for cyclic $p$-groups and the alternating group $A_4$.

papers.title: Hochschild operations and other invariants of stable equivalences of Morita type
papers.abstract:
We study stable equivalences defined by bimodule tensor identities over a commutative ring $R$. For the $R$-split exact structure, these identities preserve positive Hochschild homology and positive Hochschild cohomology with its cup product, Gerstenhaber bracket and, in prime characteristic, restricted power. A triangular comparison also identifies the relative singular Hochschild cochain complexes as $B_\infty$-algebras. For reduced pairs of finite-dimensional Frobenius algebras over an algebraically closed field, with diagonalizable Nakayama automorphisms, we construct compatible Frobenius functionals and compare the Tate--Hochschild BV operators in all degrees.
  For flat algebras over $R$ we give a Hochschild-cohomological criterion for comparing marked associative deformations. It applies to biadjoint Morita-type pairs and, by reduction, to all stable equivalences of Morita type between finite-dimensional algebras over any field. We compare the Bezrukavnikov--Ginzburg maps in characteristic zero by using a common triangular deformation or by lifting a two-sided tilting complex. We also compare marked module deformations over local Artin rings and their augmented universal rings.
  Further applications concern connected outer automorphism group schemes over perfect fields, the kernels of the quotient maps on ordinary algebraic $K$-theory, and the nonconnective $K$-theory of enhanced relative singularity categories. We construct biadjoint representatives over Henselian Noetherian local rings and relative stable tensor functors for almost $\nu$-stable derived equivalences. We also answer a question of Abe and Hoshino about preservation of the Gorenstein condition in a fixed codimension.

papers.title: Mathematical Blueprint and 240-Declaration Kernel Index for the Alpöge–Claude Lean 4 Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis
papers.abstract: On 20 November 2026, Levent Alpöge released a commentless Lean 4 formalization, developed with Claude, proving the Riemann hypothesis and the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for all Dirichlet $L$-functions across $175{,}187$ source modules ($17{,}374{,}215$ lines; $1{,}484{,}733$ compiled kernel declarations). While independent kernel replays confirm formal validity from the three standard Lean axioms, no conventional mathematical paper accompanied the archive. We give a compact, self-contained five-stage mathematical blueprint of the argument from a windowed prime-power inequality to the five root theorems of Main.lean, anchored to an index of $240$ kernel-live declarations ($233$ public declarations across $104$ modules plus $7$ structure fields and Mathlib theorems), each pinned by exact source line, kernel export_id, and five-root reachability bitmask in solution.ndjson. First, a gamma-localized Landau derivative dichotomy excludes zeros in $\operatorname{Re} s > \theta$ from a one-sided bound $G_{\mathcal{F}}(y) \le C y^\theta$ on arbitrarily distant windows $[Z, Z^{3/2}]$ without global sign assumptions. Second, character orthogonality on $G = (\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^2 \times H$ over CM towers of degree $[E:\mathbb{Q}] = 4n \asymp x^{2+8\varepsilon}$ isolates odd inert prime powers via $\mathrm{ASK} - \mathrm{MAIN} = \mathrm{De}$. Third, along an $m$-step unitary theta ladder ($m \asymp x^{1/2-\varepsilon/16}$, $k \asymp x^{9/2+10\varepsilon}$), supersingular height-$2$ Lubin-Tate formal groups supply net $\ell$-adic jet valuation rate $\gamma_\ell = \frac{1}{\ell - 1} - \frac{1}{\ell^2 - 1} = \frac{\ell}{\ell^2 - 1} = \sum_{e\,\mathrm{odd}} \ell^{-e}$ against rate $0$ at split primes. Fourth, averaging a four-clause Bost-Arakelov slope chain with Chowla-Selberg CM period evaluation cancels intermediate heights, while block-shared divisor budgets replace $O(m^2)$ prefix compounding ($x^{2/3}$ barrier) by $O(m)$; a four-wall linear program over $(a, \kappa)$ at $\nu = 2$ uniquely selects $(a, \kappa) = (1/2, 9/2)$ and $\theta_* = 1/2$. We also record three classical consequences, resolve archive homonym collisions, and verify $27$ companion algebraic, LP, Lubin-Tate, slope-telescope, and carrier-isomorphism theorems in a zero-import Lean 4.33.1 module.

papers.title: Monadicity of noncommutative measurable spaces over $C^{\ast}$-algebras
papers.abstract:
In a recent paper, Tobias Fritz and the second author identified $\sigma C^*$-algebras as a tentative noncommutative analogue of measurable spaces. We advance this analogy by establishing monadicity of $\sigma C^*$-algebras over $C^*$-algebras and proving several results of interest to both the category theory and operator algebra communities. In detail, we show that:
  - The associated probabilistic morphisms, $\sigma$-cpu maps, admit a description via a comonad closely related to the Giry monad. Equivalently, $\sigma$-cpu maps can be characterized by a universal property.
  - The category of $\sigma C^*$-algebras and $\sigma$-homomorphisms is locally $\aleph_1$-presentable.
  - $\sigma C^*$-algebras have a tensor product induced by the maximal tensor product of $C^*$-algebras and satisfying an analogous universal property.
  - The notion of CP-instruments, defined as $\sigma$-additive assignments from a $\sigma$-algebra to a space of completely positive maps, can be adapted to this setting by taking as target the set of $\sigma$-normal completely positive maps between $\sigma C^*$-algebras. This yields a bijective correspondence with $\sigma$-cpu maps out of the tensor product of the previous item.

papers.title: Classifying spaces of finite monoids with bounded homology
papers.abstract: The classifying space BM of a monoid M is the geometric realization of the nerve of M, regarded as a category with one object; its fundamental group is the universal group U(M), the group generated by the elements of M with the multiplication table of M as relations. Let M be finite. We prove that if the integral homology of BM vanishes in all large degrees, then U(M) is trivial; more precisely, if a prime p divides the order of U(M), then H_k(BM; F_p) ≠ 0 for infinitely many k. It follows that three conditions on a finite monoid are equivalent: BM is homotopy equivalent to a finite CW complex; it is homotopy equivalent to a finite-dimensional one; its homology is bounded. In that case BM is simply connected. Together with a theorem of Ben-Bassat, that every finite simply connected CW complex is homotopy equivalent to BM for a finite monoid M, this determines these homotopy types: they are the finite simply connected complexes. A conjecture of the same paper, that every connected finite CW complex with finite fundamental group is of the form BM with M finite, is therefore false; the real projective plane is a counterexample. The proof compares the K-theory of BM with that of the classifying space of a finite group contained in M, through Atiyah's completion theorem. Two examples are worked out: a monoid with six elements whose classifying space is simply connected and has homology in every degree from 2 on (it is a wedge of spheres), and a monoid with 23 elements whose classifying space is the complex projective plane.

papers.title: Cup products with volume classes in bounded cohomology
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a complete Riemannian $n$-manifold, $n\geq 2$, and suppose that either $M$ is negatively curved, or that it is a locally symmetric space of non-compact type. Via integration over straight simplices, every top-degree bounded differential form $\omega\in \Omega_b^n(M)$ defines a bounded cohomology class in $H^n_b(M)$. We prove that every such class belongs to the annihilator of the cup product in the whole graded algebra $H^{\geq 1}_b(M)$. In the case of closed orientable surfaces, this generalizes a result of Marasco, and, via transfer, provides a new proof of the fact that the cup product of the bounded Euler class of $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ with itself vanishes. Our result also applies to degree-3 bounded classes constructed by Soma and Farre, thus showing that, for surface groups and for free groups, the annihilator of the cup product is infinite dimensional also in degree 3.

papers.title: Exact, total and filtered small categories
papers.abstract: For a non-empty connected small category we compare four properties: being filtered; exactness of colimits of abelian groups; Grothendieck's total asphericity, which says that colimits of simplicial sets over the category are homotopy colimits; and being quasi-filtered, which means that two arrows with a common source can be completed to a commutative square and that two parallel arrows are equalized by an integral combination of arrows whose coefficients sum to 1. Each implies the next. We give a category of finite ordered hypergraphs that is totally aspherical and whose colimits are exact over no non-zero ring, and we show that the category of finite ordered two-graphs (sets of triples that meet every four-element set in an even number of triples) is quasi-filtered and not totally aspherical. With the example of Isbell and Mitchell, the three implications are strict. A conjecture in Grothendieck's Les Dérivateurs, that totally aspherical categories are filtered, is therefore false; it holds for sifted categories, those over which colimits of sets commute with finite products.

papers.title: Non-formality of prefactorization algebras
papers.abstract: We construct a Poisson bracket on the cohomology of locally constant prefactorization algebras on $\mathbb{R}^m$ that provides an obstruction to formality in every dimension $m\geqslant 2$. Our construction combines colored obstruction sequences to formality with linking spheres and generalizes the two-dimensional bracket of Bruinsma, Schenkel, and Vicedo. We use it to extend their non-formality theorem for Lie algebra factorization envelopes to all higher dimensions. We also establish new non-formality results for factorization envelopes of Lie algebras, their compactifications and generalizations to $L_\infty$-algebras, free BF-type theories, higher abelian Chern-Simons theories and their compactifications.

papers.title: One monoid to realize them all: a master monoid for homotopy types
papers.abstract:
Homotopy theory has traditionally been approached either through topological spaces or through categories of presheaves on suitable combinatorial categories, a perspective subsumed by Grothendieck's theory of test categories. In this paper, we develop a more algebraic viewpoint: homotopy types can be represented by actions of a single monoid on sets.
  This monoid is obtained by identifying all the objects of the semisimplicial category while retaining its face operators. Every CW homotopy type is the classifying space of the translation category of one of its actions, and its truncation at dimension n is finitely presented and realizes exactly the homotopy types of dimension at most n.
  The construction rests on a general result: every set-valued functor on a small category freely generates an action of its universal monoid, and its category of elements is a full coreflective subcategory of the resulting translation category. Hence every weak test category gives rise to a monoid whose actions realize all homotopy types; when the category has more than one object, however, this monoid is not itself a weak test category, so that a single monoid may realize all homotopy types without modelling homotopy theory as a localization. The obstruction lies in identifying objects, not in having a single one: there are strict test categories with a single object, such as the monoid of all self-maps of an infinite set and a countable monoid of primitive recursive functions.

papers.title: Products and duality for framed 1-flow categories
papers.abstract: We describe a product between framed 1-flow categories and show that it satisfies the expected Cartan formula on its second Steenrod squares. We also describe a dual framed 1-flow category and show that, like the Spanier-Whitehead dual of spectra, the homology groups of a framed 1-flow category can be shown to be isomorphic to the cohomology groups of its dual and that this isomorphism can be shown to cooperate with the framed 1-flow category structure in a suitable sense.

papers.title: Second homotopy modules and infinite homotopy stable classes of four-manifolds
papers.abstract: We construct infinitely many closed oriented smooth 4-manifolds which are all stably diffeomorphic but pairwise not homotopy equivalent. Our examples are distinguished by their second homotopy modules, and provide the first examples which demonstrate that stable diffeomorphism does not determine the second homotopy module. They have fundamental group $(\mathbb{Z}/4)^4*\mathbb{Z}$ and arise as doubles of presentation 2-complexes. In contrast, we give criteria for isomorphism of second homotopy modules of doubles of 2-complexes, covering finite abelian, quaternion, dihedral and symmetric fundamental groups. We also establish non-injectivity of the doubling construction by showing that there exist homotopically distinct presentation 2-complexes over $Q_{28}$ whose doubles are homotopy equivalent.

papers.title: The first L²-Betti number of aspherical manifolds and Poincaré duality groups of dimension at least three
papers.abstract: The L²-Betti numbers b_p⁽²⁾ of a finite complex measure the square-summable harmonic p-chains on its universal cover. Singer's conjecture says that for a closed aspherical manifold of dimension n, one whose universal cover is contractible, they vanish outside the middle degree n/2. A manuscript of OpenAI dated 25 September 2026, released on 6 October 2026, proves the conjecture in dimension four; it is not refereed. Its proof assumes b₁⁽²⁾ > 0, builds from functions of finite energy on the fundamental group Γ a compact boundary on which Γ acts, and reaches a contradiction; dimension four enters only in a preliminary section. We show that the same argument gives b₁⁽²⁾ = b_{n−1}⁽²⁾ = 0 for every finite aspherical Poincaré complex of formal dimension n ≥ 3, hence for every closed aspherical topological manifold of dimension at least three (Theorem A), and for every finitely presented Poincaré duality group of dimension n ≥ 3 (Theorem B). To do so we state what Sections 3-10 of the manuscript prove as a criterion for groups (Theorem C): a finitely presented torsion-free group with one end, with H²(Γ; F₂Γ) = 0 and with no splitting over a finite or two-ended subgroup, has b₁⁽²⁾ = 0; and we prove, in every dimension n ≥ 3, the facts about Γ that the criterion needs. Theorems A and B depend on the manuscript's argument, which we cite and do not reproduce. One AI referee has followed that argument line by line and found no fault; no human has checked it, or this paper.

papers.title: The profinite Grothendieck-Teichmüller monoid is a group, on a question of Lochak and Schneps
papers.abstract: An element of the profinite Grothendieck-Teichmüller group $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$ of Drinfeld is a pair $(\lambda,f)$, with $\lambda$ a unit of $\widehat{\mathbb Z}$ and $f$ in the free profinite group $\widehat F_2$ on $x$ and $y$, that satisfies three relations and for which $x\mapsto x^\lambda$, $y\mapsto f^{-1}y^\lambda f$ is an automorphism of $\widehat F_2$. Lochak and Schneps asked in 2006 whether this last requirement follows from the others, and whether it holds with no relation at all (Question 1.1 of their list of open problems). We prove that it follows, and from less: if $\lambda\in1+2\widehat{\mathbb Z}$ and $f\in\widehat F_2$ satisfy the two-cycle and three-cycle relations (I) and (II), then $\lambda$ is a unit and the endomorphism is an automorphism. The pentagon relation is not used. Relation (I) alone does not suffice: for $\lambda=1$ and $f=xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$ the endomorphism is not surjective. It follows that the Grothendieck-Teichmüller monoid, in the profinite form of Horel and of Boavida de Brito, Horel and Robertson, is equal to its group of units; that every endomorphism of the profinite operad of parenthesized braids that fixes the objects is an automorphism; and, by their theorems, that every homotopy endomorphism of the profinite completion of the little 2-discs operad, or of the genus zero surface operad, is a homotopy automorphism. The proof counts boundary components of finite covers in homology. An endomorphism of the profinite completion of the fundamental group of a compact surface with boundary that sends every boundary generator to a conjugate of a unit power of a boundary generator, bijectively on boundary components, is an automorphism; on a sphere with at least three holes the exponents of such an endomorphism are equal, and are zero or a unit. The criterion for unit exponents and the case of unit $\lambda$ were produced by GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode) and checked by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort high. Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max checked them again, found the statements for exponents that are not assumed to be units and the example above, and wrote this text. Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max checked these additions independently. No human has checked any of it.

papers.title: Topological Inference for degree-Cech complexes
papers.abstract: We study topological inference for the degree-Cech bifiltration from noisy samples of a manifold. Under a model combining uniform sampling on the manifold with uniform noise, we show that suitable choices of the radius and degree parameters recover the homotopy type of the underlying manifold with high probability. The analysis explains how the degree parameter suppresses sufficiently distant outliers while the radius scale captures topological signals. Our results provide theoretical support for the common intuition that degree bifiltrations carry meaningful topological information in the presence of noise.

papers.title: Twisted $L^2$-torsion functions obstruct fibring over the circle
papers.abstract: The vanishing of the L^2-Betti numbers of the universal covering of a closed manifold is an obstruction to fibring over the circle. When the L^2-Betti numbers vanish we introduce a secondary obstruction based on the asymptotic behaviour of the twisted L^2-torsion function at 0 and infinity. We provide a number of examples showing the invariant is indeed non-trivial.

papers.title: A short proof of Serre positivity
papers.abstract: Recently, OpenAI found a proof of the positivity of Serre's intersection multiplicity. The two main ingredients are a descent result on rational $K$-theory with support; and a construction of certain category of asymptotic complexes that identifies with the category of perfect complexes over a connective (non-commutative) derived ring. In this article, we present a simpler proof of Serre positivity that circumvents the second step; instead, we use a ``reduction to the diagonal" trick via the $A_{\text{inf}}$-construction.

papers.title: A constant gap for the maximal cp-rank
papers.abstract: We prove that the maximal cp-rank $p_N$ of completely positive matrices of order $N$ satisfies $p_N=N^2/2-N/2+O(1)$. More precisely, we prove $p_N\leq\binom{N}{2}$ for every $N\geq3$ using an analytic argument based on coordinate scaling. A computer-assisted construction gives $p_N\geq\binom{N}{2}-2$ for $14\leq N\leq208$ and for every larger $N\not\equiv1\pmod4$. In the remaining residue class, it gives $p_N\geq\binom{N}{2}-3$.

papers.title: A Higgs category for the cluster variety of triples of flags
papers.abstract: The cluster variety of triples of flags (associated with a split simple Lie group of Dynkin type Delta) plays a key role in higher Teichmuller theory as developed by Fock-Goncharov, Jiarui Fei, Ian Le, ... and Goncharov-Shen. We refer to it as the basic triangle associated with Delta. In this paper, for simply laced Delta, we construct and study a Higgs category (in the sense of Yilin Wu) which we expect to categorify the basic triangle. This category is a certain exact dg category (in the sense of Xiaofa Chen) which is Frobenius and stably 2-Calabi-Yau. We show that it has indeed the expected cyclic group symmetry and that its derived category has the expected braid group symmetry. A key ingredient in our construction is a conjecture by Merlin Christ, whose proof occupies most of this paper. The proof is based on a new description of the Higgs category in terms of Gorenstein projective dg modules. Our techniques are in the spirit of Orlov in his work on triangulated categories of graded B-branes.

papers.title: A Lower Bound for the Pyjama Problem
papers.abstract: Let $N(\varepsilon)$ be the least number of rotations of the periodic stripe $\{(x,y):\operatorname{dist}(x,\Z)\le\varepsilon\}$ that cover the plane. We prove that $\varepsilon N(\varepsilon)\to\infty$ as $\varepsilon\to0$, answering a question of Li. More precisely, for each fixed $C>0$, $n$ stripe families in distinct directions with half-width $C/n$ leave an area fraction $e^{-2C}+o(1)$ uncovered. The error is uniform in the directions and their translations.

papers.title: A Machine-Certified Degree-2,799 Counterexample to Smale's Mean Value Conjecture via Envelope-Theorem Barycentric Minimax Optimization and pandroots
papers.abstract: We construct and unconditionally machine-certify an explicit complex polynomial p(u) in Q(i)[u] of exact degree d = 2,799 satisfying p(0) = 0, p'(0) = 1, and min_{p'(zeta)=0} |p(zeta)/zeta| in [1.0002520813917934477351916, 1.0002520813917934477351917] > 1, setting a new lowest-degree record for explicit counterexamples to Smale's 1981 Mean Value Conjecture (K <= 1). Compared with the October 2026 disproof of Adamczewski and Colbrook (arXiv:2610.36158, degree 29,984, minimum ~1.000000495958) and our November 24, 2026 record (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.24512942, degree 7,299, minimum ~1.000027196554), the new construction reduces the certified degree by 10.71x and 2.61x respectively, while increasing the certified margin above 1 by 508.3x and 9.27x. By standard leading-term perturbation, counterexamples exist for every degree n >= 2,799. To break through the ~7,300 degree floor of pure analytic conformal-map interpolation, we introduce Envelope-Theorem barycentric minimax optimization in the O(log M)-conditioned Fejer-Lagrange nodal basis with a free anchor a in C and iterative bootstrap degree compression coupled with Maehly's deflated Newton root tracking. The compact 1.3 MB exact Gaussian-integer polynomial with exact 15-bit dyadic anchor a = (22901 - 11056*i) / 2^15 is certified with zero floating-point assumptions in 10.43 s on 10 CPU cores by combining pandroots v0.31.0 (certify_roots_exact, 8.56 s, max radius 2^-795) with an exact BigInt Smale ratio enclosure (1.85 s), independently verified at 700-digit precision in Python mpmath and reproduced on GitHub Actions CI. Code and green CI: https://github.com/ivan-fr/smale-deg2799 | Zenodo DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.24531472.

papers.title: A Machine-Certified Degree-7,299 Counterexample to Smale's Mean Value Conjecture
papers.abstract: We construct and rigorously machine-certify an explicit polynomial p in Q(i)[z] of degree d = 7,299 with p(0) = 0 and p'(0) = 1 such that all 7,298 critical points satisfy min_{p'(c)=0} |p(c)/c| in [1.00002719655422710959, 1.00002719655422710960] > 1. This reduces the lowest known rigorously certified counterexample degree for Smale's Mean Value Conjecture by a factor of 4.11x compared to the October 2026 breakthrough of Adamczewski and Colbrook (degree 29,984), while increasing the margin above 1 by 54.8x. The polynomial is constructed via an analytic Fourier-smoothed Pac-Man conformal map, Fejér-Lagrange interpolation, and bit-reversal equidistribution, and verified with zero floating-point assumptions in exact arbitrary-precision integer arithmetic alongside independent 900-digit mpmath checks and pandroots v0.31.0.

papers.title: A nine-line counterexample to a conjecture on the minimal degree of Jacobian relations
papers.abstract: We construct two arrangements of nine lines in the complex projective plane with isomorphic intersection lattices, of weak combinatorics $(n_2,n_3,n_4)=(9,7,1)$, whose defining equations $f$ and $g$ satisfy $${\rm mdr}(f)=4,\qquad {\rm mdr}(g)=5.$$ Since $4<9/2$, this disproves a conjecture of the first author which would have implied Terao's Conjecture on the combinatorial nature of the freeness of line arrangements. Equivalently, the rank two vector bundle of logarithmic vector fields is strictly semistable for the first arrangement and stable for the second one. Hence the stability of this bundle is not determined by the intersection lattice, which gives a counterexample to a conjecture of Abe. The two arrangements also have different minimal free resolutions of their Milnor algebras. All computations are exact, and a short SINGULAR script performing them is included.

papers.title: A planar graph without four- or nine-cycles that is not three-colorable
papers.abstract: We give an 82-vertex planar graph without cycles of length four or nine that is not three-colorable. Steinberg conjectured in 1976 that planar graphs without cycles of length four or five are three-colorable; Cohen-Addad, Hebdige, Král', Li and Salgado disproved this, and their graph contains a nine-cycle. Lu, Wang, Wang, Bu, Montassier and Raspaud asked, as recorded by Kang, Jin and Wang, for which lengths from five to nine every planar graph without cycles of that length or of length four is three-colorable. Our graph answers the length-nine case negatively. It is built from 27 complete graphs on four vertices by Ore compositions, the edge-deletion and vertex-splitting operation of Dirac, Hajós, Gallai and Ore. It is four-critical: every proper subgraph is three-colorable. Its 136 edges attain Kostochka and Yancey's lower bound, so no four-critical graph on 82 vertices has fewer edges. Lean checks planarity, the exclusion of four- and nine-cycles, and non-three-colorability; criticality and the edge minimum rest on the written proof. This work has not yet been reviewed by experts. The proofs, the Lean formalization, the search code, the certificate checkers and the text were produced by AI models, working under the author's direction.

papers.title: A smooth compactification of similarity classes of triangles
papers.abstract: We provide a smooth algebraic compactification of the space of labeled, oriented similarity classes of triangles, as a quotient of a 3-point configuration space in the plane -- minus triple-collisions -- by the similarity group. The configuration space is naturally isomorphic to the Fulton-MacPherson space of \cite{FM94} and to the Schubert-Semple space of \cite{Semple}. The quotient is topologically a connected sum of three projective planes, and projects via blow-down to two shape spaces that have appeared in the literature: the well-known 2-sphere (\cite{Kend84}, \cite{Beh}, \cite{Montgomery}, \cite{ES15}), and the less-well-known 2-torus (\cite{BG23}). A natural action by the dihedral group $D_6$ yields a quotient stack describing absolute (unlabeled, unoriented) triangle classes.

papers.title: A Solution to the Gerstenhaber Problem for Three Commuting Matrices
papers.abstract: Three pairwise commuting endomorphisms of an n-dimensional vector space generate a unital algebra of dimension at most n. The bound holds over every field and is sharp in every dimension. The proof fixes the number of Jordan blocks of one generator and allows their lengths to vary. A violation of the bound would give a pole of a determinantal minor. Along its divisor the second generator would act without a cyclic vector both on the cokernel and on the kernel of the first, after the first has been shifted to a nilpotent operator. These two conditions confine the image of the divisor under a finite map to a set of codimension at least two.

papers.title: A uniform spectral gap and winding-flux tension on the SU(2) plaquette ladder
papers.abstract: For the periodic one-plaquette-wide SU(2) Kogut–Susskind ladder at fixed lattice spacing and every even length L ≥ 2, we give a computer-assisted argument for a full spectral gap exceeding one fundamental-link electric energy throughout 0 ≤ x = λ/e ≤ 12.25, and exceeding 0.46 through x = 16. All link representations are retained. The winding-sector ground-energy difference per plaquette has an even-length thermodynamic limit. It is at least 0.5584 through x = 12, at least 0.20 through x = 30, and at least 0.1425 through x = 32. A plaquette-product trial gives an exact variational bound at arbitrary length. The spectral estimates combine a split-link reflection construction, finite-ring interval enclosures and Lean certificates. The physical realization of the formal hypotheses and the cutoff limit are paper arguments.

papers.title: Abelian envelopes and quantum groups in Knop's interpolation categories
papers.abstract: We show the existence of abelian envelopes for large classes of subcategories of Knop's tensor envelopes. It follows that these abelian envelopes correspond to groups or more generally Hopf algebras (``quantum groups'') in their parent interpolation categories. As a special case, we obtain that the interpolation categories in the sense of Flake--Maassen (2022) of all so-called group-theoretical easy quantum groups have abelian envelopes given by quantum groups in Deligne's interpolation category of the symmetric groups. Similarly, we apply our theory to interpolation categories of wreath products, finite general linear groups, and finite affine groups. Our main technique is an explicit construction of objects corresponding to coordinate algebras using the calculus of relations that Knop's categories are based on.

papers.title: Additive basis thresholds for random prime semigroups
papers.abstract: Admit $2$ and select each odd prime $q$ independently with probability $\min(1,\lambda q^{-\gamma})$. We study sums from the multiplicative semigroup generated by the selected primes. At $\lambda=1$, its least asymptotic basis order is almost surely $\lfloor(1-\gamma)^{-1}\rfloor+1$ for $0<\gamma<1$. On the critical line $\gamma=1-1/k$, the multiplier threshold for cofiniteness of the $k$-fold sumset is $1+1/k$. At equality the probability of cofiniteness is strictly between zero and one. Almost every realization at equality admits a finite addition of primes that makes its $k$-fold sumset cofinite and a finite removal of optional primes that gives infinitely many gaps. The proof combines a lower sieve and a prime-support overlap estimate for representations with a stopped martingale that compensates surviving gaps.

papers.title: Affine standard Lyndon words
papers.abstract: In this note, we establish the convexity and monotonicity for affine standard Lyndon words in all types, generalizing the $A$-type results of arXiv:2305.16299. We also derive partial results on the structure of imaginary standard Lyndon words and present a conjecture for their general form. Additionally, we provide computer code in Appendix that, in particular, allows to efficiently compute affine standard Lyndon words in exceptional types for all orders.

papers.title: An automatically generated exposition of the Casimir bound casBound_holds in Alpöge's Lean proof of the Riemann hypothesis
papers.abstract: Levent Alpöge's Lean archive contains a tableau bound for the quadratic Casimir on column-alternating tensors. This automatically generated exposition explains his existing theorem casBound_holds and its coordinate proof. Its contribution is expository. The theorem bounds the real quadratic form of the slot Casimir on a union of whole columns by the squared tensor norm times an explicit coefficient in the tableau label multiplicities. Alpöge's proof bounds the swaps from one outside box into a column together, using one squared norm, and then counts the contributions by label. An AI-run survey found no explanation of the theorem in nine write-ups of the proof. On a separate theorem, typePrimesN, two independent AI graders found that the pipeline captured seven of eight insights in a hidden key before review and all eight after revision, with no incorrect keyed insights in either version.

papers.title: An Improved Lower Bound S(3, t) >= 3t - 4 for Positive Solutions of Bivariate Trinomial-t-nomial Systems and an Explicit Degree-45 Eight-Root Example
papers.abstract: Let S(3, t) denote the maximum number of isolated strictly positive real solutions in R_{>0}^2 of a real bivariate polynomial system f(x, y) = g(x, y) = 0 where f is a trinomial (3 monomials) and g is a t-nomial (t >= 3 monomials). We prove by an elementary, Sard-free constructive induction that S(3, t) >= 3t - 4 for every integer t >= 3, matching Haas's sharp value S(3, 3) = 5, strictly improving the 2007 Gomez-Niles-Rojas bound 2t - 1 for every t >= 4, and increasing the asymptotic lower-bound slope by 50%. We also exhibit a compact, symmetric degree-45 integer system of type (3, 4), x^8 + y^8 - 1 = 0 and 8x^45 + 8y^45 + 35x^3 y^3 - 25xy = 0, with 8 simple strictly positive roots, plus explicit integer records for (3, 5) (11 roots) and (3, 6) (14 roots). Both main theorems (including nondegeneracy det J != 0 for all t >= 3) are formally verified in Lean 4.36.0 (Mathlib4, 2,404 lines, zero sorry, standard axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] only) with green GitHub Actions CI, alongside three independent computational certifications (exact BigInt IVT, pandsysroots v0.33.0, and 200-digit mpmath).

papers.title: An Introduction to O-minimal Geometry
papers.abstract: These lecture notes on o-minimal geometry comprise six chapters: 1 - O minimal Structures. 2 - Cell Decomposition. 3 - Connected Components and Dimension. 4 - Definable Triangulation. 5 - Generic Fibers for Definable Families. 6 - Smoothness.

papers.title: An Introduction to Semialgebraic Geometry
papers.abstract: The first chapter of these lecture notes explains algorithms for counting real roots and the Tarski-Seidenberg theorem. In the next two chapters we study semialgebraic subsets of $\mathbb R^n$ , which are defined by boolean combinations of polynomial equations and inequalities. The main tool for this study is the cylindrical algebraic decomposition, which is introduced in Chapter 2. The principal result of Chapter 3 is the triangulation theorem. This theorem shows that semialgebraic sets have a simple topology, which can be effectively computed from their definitions. Chapter 4 contains examples of finiteness results and uniform bounds for semialgebraic families. In particular, we give an explicit bound for the number of connected components of a real algebraic set as a function of the degree of the equations and the dimension of the ambient space.

papers.title: Area Rigidity for the Regular Representation of Surface Groups
papers.abstract: Let $\tilde{\Sigma}$ be the universal cover of a closed surface $\Sigma$ of genus at least $2$. We characterize all equivariantly area-minimizing maps from $\tilde{\Sigma}$ to a Hilbert sphere, which are equivariant with respect to an isometric action of $\pi_1(\Sigma)$ weakly equivalent to the regular representation. As part of our proof, we classify all totally isotropic minimal surfaces in Hilbert spheres with constant negative Gaussian curvature. This builds on earlier results of E. Calabi, K. Kenmotsu, R. Bryant.

papers.title: Arithmetic Siegel-Weil formulas for unitary Shimura varieties with Iwahori levels
papers.abstract: In this paper, we formulate conjectural formulas for the arithmetic intersection numbers of special cycles on unitary Shimura varieties with Iwahori level structure. We first introduce a framework for formulating Kudla-Rapoport conjectures: we develop the theory of weighted representation densities and special cycles for general parahoric level structures, prove dimension-reduction formulas on both the analytic and geometric sides and duality relations for special cycles. We then formulate the Kudla-Rapoport conjecture for Iwahori level structures based on these properties. Finally, we prove the conjecture when $n=2$.

papers.title: Binary Minor Certificates for the $\mathcal A(1)$-hit problem of $MO(2)$
papers.abstract: Let $M=\widetilde H^*(MO(2);\mathbb F_2)$ and let $\mathcal A(1)$ be the subalgebra of the mod $2$ Steenrod algebra generated by $\operatorname{Sq}^1$ and $\operatorname{Sq}^2$. In this work, we determine the quotient $\mathbb F_2\otimes_{\mathcal A(1)}M$ in every internal degree $h\geq0$, where internal degree $h$ corresponds to cohomological degree $h+2$. To overcome the limitations of finite experimental extrapolation, our proof is strictly certifying: in each degree, we exhibit a determinant-one minor of the binary hit matrix and a complementary family of linear dual functionals annihilating every hit column, mathematically guaranteeing the exact rank for all degrees. This rigorously establishes the monomial generating families and module decomposition proposed in Shih's 2012 report. Furthermore, we derive a closed binomial formula for every Steenrod square from the length-two symmetric-polynomial model, correct a boundary omission in the $\mathcal A(0)$ calculation, compute the exact Hilbert series of the $\mathcal A(1)$-cohit, and prove an intrinsic direct-sum decomposition of $M$ into two stable $\mathcal A(1)$-submodules.

papers.title: Bloch Discriminants of Discrete Periodic Operators
papers.abstract: The Bloch variety of an operator on a periodic graph encodes the relation between its spectrum and the group action on the graph, with critical points corresponding to edges of the spectrum. We adapt methods from computational algebraic geometry to describe how the qualitative behavior of critical points of Bloch varieties depends upon parameters for three Z^2-periodic graphs. The set of parameters where the qualitative behavior changes is the Bloch discriminant. As the critical points are real-algebraic with respect to a non-standard real structure on the complex torus, this is also a first step towards developing computational tools for varieties with a non-standard real structure.

papers.title: Boundedness and Kawamata-Viehweg vanishing for threefolds of Fano type in large characteristics
papers.abstract: We study threefolds over algebraically closed fields of large positive characteristic. Let \((X,B)\) be a projective log canonical pair with \(X\) of Fano type, \(-(K_X+B)\) nef and coefficients of \(B\) in a fixed hyperstandard set. We obtain a monotonic complement of bounded index. For exceptional pairs the complement is Kawamata log terminal. We prove that all \(\epsilon\)-log canonical weak log Fano threefolds are arithmetically bounded above a characteristic threshold independent of \(\epsilon\). We also prove Kawamata--Viehweg vanishing for integral \(\Q\)-Cartier Weil divisors on projective threefolds of Fano type above an absolute characteristic threshold.

papers.title: Boundedness of complements for fibered Fano threefolds in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove a canonical bundle formula for Fano type fibrations and Shokurov's conjecture on boundedness of complements for Fano type threefold pairs $(X,B)$ with fibration structures in large characteristics. In particular, we prove the conjecture when $-(K_X+B)\not\equiv 0$ is nef and not big in large characteristics.

papers.title: Brauer classes of representations of division algebras and their Langlands parameters
papers.abstract: For every depth-zero supercuspidal representation $\pi$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n(K)$ with algebraic-valued central character, we prove that the Brauer obstructions to realizing its Jacquet-Langlands transfer and its normalized Langlands parameter $\varphi_\pi\otimes|\cdot|^{-(n-1)/2}$ over their common field of rationality $E=\mathbb{Q}(\pi)$ sum to $(n-1)[B_{p,\infty}\otimes_{\mathbb{Q}} E]$. Here $K/\mathbb{Q}_p$ is finite, the transfer is to the units of the central division algebra over $K$ of invariant $1/n$, and $B_{p,\infty}$ is the quaternion algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$ ramified exactly at $p$ and $\infty$. We conjecture this identity without the depth restriction. For arbitrarily large $n=p-1$, we construct simple supercuspidal representations satisfying the same sum formula. Their transfers have finite-order central character and Schur index $n$, whereas their normalized parameters have index $n/2$. Since these transfers are not self-dual, the unequal indices contradict the isomorphism of Schur algebras conjectured by Prasad and Ramakrishnan.

papers.title: Central algebraic cohomology of Galois gerbes and its abelianization
papers.abstract: We study central algebraic cohomology and its abelianization for Galois gerbes over local fields of characteristic zero and over number fields. The coefficients consist of a connected reductive group and a central subgroup that need not be finite or connected. We construct a canonical abelian group structure on abelian central cohomology. When the gerbe admits a morphism from Kaletha's rigid gerbe, we obtain a fiber product formula for this group in terms of rigid cohomology and homomorphisms from the band to the central subgroup. Over number fields, abelianization and localization at the real places recover the full central cohomology set. We obtain explicit formulas for Kottwitz's local and global gerbes and for Fargues's extended Kottwitz gerbe.

papers.title: Characteristic-Free Skew-Symmetric Classical Invariant Theor
papers.abstract:
We study an exterior-algebra analogue of classical invariant theory for linear, symplectic, and orthogonal groups, with particular emphasis on integral constructions and positive characteristic.
  The theory presented here is rather different from the classical one developed by us in DeConcini Procesi 1976 .
  In fact, the present theory is based on good filtrations and on a surprising divided-power structure on the algebras of exterior invariants.
  We also include a short characteristic-zero treatment of the corresponding First and Second Fundamental Theorems via the exterior Cauchy identity; these known results motivate the integral theory.

papers.title: Chern classes of vanishing cycles for maps having no blowups
papers.abstract: We study the nearby and vanishing cycles for maps with no blowups. For holomorphic maps between complex manifolds admitting at most ICIS, we show that the Riemann-Hurwitz defect in Chern classes is compensated for by the Chern class transformation of the Milnor number constructible function.

papers.title: Constructive Folded-Haas Trinomial Systems and Exponential Lower Bounds on Fewnomial Root Counts
papers.abstract: Let B(n, k) denote the maximum number of nondegenerate strictly positive real solutions to a square system of n polynomial equations in n variables supported on at most n + k + 1 distinct monomials. Since Bihan, Rojas, and Sottile (2007), the general lower bound B(n, k) >= floor((n + k)/k)^k has stood as the standard benchmark across all dimensions n and codimensions k, proved via a nonconstructive product of k copies of Bihan's k = 1 theorem. In this paper we establish three constructive advances, all realized exclusively by explicit trinomial polynomial systems and completely formalized in Lean 4 (v4.36.0, Mathlib4) with zero unproved axioms: (1) Explicit sharp k = 1 trinomial systems attaining B(n, 1) = n + 1 for every n >= 1 (solving Bihan-Rojas-Sottile Remark 2); (2) Folded-Haas k = 2 trinomial systems yielding B(n, 2) >= 5 * floor((n+2)/4) * floor((n+4)/4) = (5/16) n^2 + O(n), improving the 2007 bound (1/4) n^2 + O(n) by 25% asymptotically and giving explicit new records B(4,2) >= 10, B(6,2) >= 20, B(8,2) >= 30, B(10,2) >= 45, and B(14,2) >= 80; (3) An exponential improvement for every codimension k >= 2, achieving (5/4)^floor(k/2) * floor((n + k)/k)^k nondegenerate positive roots at n = k(2m - 1). All three theorems are machine-checked in Lean 4.36.0 using only standard axioms, and concrete primal polynomial systems are independently certified via polyhedral homotopy (pandsysroots v0.33.0) and 220-digit arbitrary-precision verification.

papers.title: Convolution Algebras of Generalized Preprojective Algebras and Kac-Moody Positive Parts
papers.abstract: We realize the enveloping algebras of positive parts of symmetrizable Kac-Moody Lie algebras as convolution algebras of constructible functions on module varieties of Geiss-Leclerc-Schr\"oer generalized preprojective algebras $\Pi(C,D)$. We characterize all pairs $(C,D)$ for which such a realization exists. These realizations generalize Lusztig's classical preprojective construction. The construction uses a folding embedding and torus actions on flag varieties.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the positivity and saturation hypotheses of GCT VI
papers.abstract: Part VI of Mulmuley's geometric complexity theory formulates three hypotheses on the stretching quasi-polynomials of Kronecker coefficients, plethysm coefficients and, more generally, multiplicities of subgroup restriction: the saturation index (SH) and the positivity index (PH2) should be bounded by a polynomial in the size of the input, and the generating function should admit a positive rational form whose largest denominator exponent, the modular index, is bounded by such a polynomial (PH3). We show that these hypotheses fail. For every n ≥ 2 the series Σ_{s≥0} g((sⁿ),(sⁿ),(sⁿ)) tˢ of triple-rectangular Kronecker coefficients has a pole at a primitive root of unity of order 2ⁿ⁻¹3ʳ for some r ≥ 0, so every positive rational form, indeed every expression P(t)/∏ᵢ(1 − t^{aᵢ})^{bᵢ}, has some aᵢ ≥ 2ⁿ⁻¹, while the input rank is n² + 5n; this refutes the existence clause of PH3 for Kronecker coefficients, also in the relaxed form that Mulmuley gave in the appendix to the paper of Briand, Orellana and Rosas. The proof reduces modulo three to the cyclic permutation of the three tensor factors, whose trace is the Hilbert series of the invariants of ℂⁿ ⊕ 𝕊_(2,1)ℂⁿ, and locates there a unique fixed curve of the grading group μ_{2ⁿ⁻¹}. For the plethysm coefficients of Sym^d(Sym³ ℂⁿ) along the ray of the determinant, the Hilbert series has simple poles at the primitive 2ⁿ⁻¹-th roots of unity for every n ≥ 4, which refutes PH3; a signed trace of these poles dominates all other terms, which gives positivity and saturation indices larger than 2^{cn} for every c < 1/4 and all large n, refuting PH2 and SH(a). Both arguments rest on a support theorem for cubic forms: a diagonal matrix of two-power order fixing a semistable cubic in n variables has determinant of order at most 2ⁿ⁻¹, with equality only for the chain cubic x₁²x₂ + ⋯ + x²_{n−1}xₙ + xₙ³. For restriction from a rank-one torus, which GCT VI admits as an explicit embedding, the three hypotheses fail at a fixed input rank.

papers.title: Counting periodic points of rational self-maps of projective varieties
papers.abstract:
We study the asymptotic behaviour of the number of isolated periodic points of a dominant rational self-map of a smooth projective variety. We first give an upper bound for this number in terms of the degrees of the iterates of the map, thereby extending a theorem of Dinh--Nguyen--Truong to arbitrary characteristic. Our approach is purely algebraic and bypasses the theory of densities of positive closed currents.
  We then establish the exact asymptotic growth of isolated periodic points of birational self-maps of surfaces over a field of characteristic 0. To do so, we extend Jonsson--Reschke's argument to any finitely generated field over $ \mathbb Q $ using Moriwaki's theory of heights.

papers.title: Cyclic source pairings for Penrose--Sparling non-Hausdorff twistor spaces
papers.abstract: We determine the stable source information carried by the gluing-groupoid algebra of the Penrose--Sparling non-Hausdorff twistor double. Relative normal residues define supported analytic $K$-classes with specified normal orientations. For a smooth double along a closed submanifold, we compute the full geometric periodic cyclic homology as the parity sum of the compactly supported cohomologies of the ambient manifold and the doubled locus. In the physical model, $K_0\cong\Z^4$ and $HP_0\cong\C^4$, with both odd groups zero. Four explicit cocycles give integral $K$-coordinates and exhaust continuous periodic cyclic cohomology; every periodic cyclic pairing on supported source classes is therefore a linear combination of rank and degree. Finite moments recover $K$-valued normal profiles modulo integral common line twists. A first-jet criterion tests mixed-line triviality and identifies the residue with the torsion cokernel of a generically invertible second fundamental form for pullback quotients. The degree-one Euler modification and the diagonal Coulomb embedding have identical filtered $K$-profiles in every algebraic $SL_2$ representation, while their rank-two Ward connections are respectively indecomposable and split. We give the Euler connection and its transition between both root charts. An elementary holonomy realization shows that the inherited ambient and divisor transverse classes annihilate supported source classes. The relative degree pairing uses an additional choice of opposite defect orientations.

papers.title: Derivations of Low-Dimensional Filiform Lie Superalgebras
papers.abstract: We determine the even and odd derivations of the 91 entries in Gilg's classification list of complex filiform Lie superalgebras of superdimensions (2|2), (2|3), (2|4), (3|2), (3|3), (4|2), (5|2) and (6|2). A unified linear system yields explicit matrix parametrizations and the dimensions of both homogeneous components of the derivation superalgebra. The results are given in block-matrix form.

papers.title: Eisenstein Cohomology and Critical Values of Certain \(L\)-Functions: A Root-Theoretic Combinatorial Lemma
papers.abstract:
This paper gives a root-theoretic extension of the Harder--Raghuram combinatorial lemma, relating criticality of adjacent $L-$values to degrees in nilradical cohomology, to maximal parabolics $P=MU$ of connected split reductive groups with irreducible, essentially tempered cohomological inducing data.
  At real places, the paper classifies the maximal parabolics for which the two Kostant degrees in the boundary comparison can agree at a regular shift. For each such parabolic, an admissible shift makes both adjacent arguments critical in every Langlands--Shahidi grade exactly when both Kostant degrees equal $\dim U/2$. The classification recovers the two-block parabolics of type $A$ with even product of block sizes (Harder--Raghuram, proved by Weselmann) and the isotropic-line parabolic of type $D_{2m+1}$ for $m\ge2$ (Bhagwat--Raghuram). The only exceptional cases are $P_1$ and $P_6$ of type $E_6$. In all other cases, roots of $U$ fixed by the longest Levi Weyl element confine simultaneous criticality to a singular wall, generalizing the odd-block obstruction for $\mathrm{GL}_N$. Their number is the difference of the fundamental ranks of $M$ and $G$. When the Kostant degrees differ, as in Harder's $\mathrm{GL}_2$ setting, the paper determines which boundary degrees can still coincide.
  At a complex place, an admissible shift is simultaneously critical exactly when the two conjugate Levi weights after the shift occur in Kostant degrees summing to $\dim U$. With a common relative center, total degree balance at a regular admissible shift characterizes simultaneous criticality at every archimedean place. For split $E_6$ over $\mathbb Q$, a half-spin family yields Eisenstein cohomology classes in degrees $20$ and $21$, including a degree-$20$ class with nonzero restrictions to both associate boundary face types.

papers.title: Equivariant Levi restriction
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group over $\bbC$, $L\subset G$ a Levi subgroup, and $\cL\subset\cG$ their Langlands duals. Macerato \cite{macerato2023leviequivariantrestrictionsphericalperverse} computed the $\cL(\calO)$-equivariant cohomology of the $!$-restriction to $\GrL$ of the regular spherical perverse sheaf on $\GrG$, and identified it with the functions on the partial Kostant--Whittaker reduction $T^*(G/U,\psiL)$, where $\psiL$ is the possibly degenerate Whittaker character of $U$ determined by $L$. We add loop rotation. Our main result is: the $\LO$-equivariant cohomology of the same object is the ring $\Dh(G/U,\psiL)$ of asymptotic $\psiL$-twisted differential operators on $G/U$. For a single $\IC_V$ the answer is the space of intertwiners $\bM_\hbar(\psiL)\to V\otimes\bM_\hbar(\psiL)$ of the universal Verma--Whittaker module. This interpolates between results of Bezrukavnikov--Finkelberg ($L=G$) and Ginzburg--Riche ($L=T$).

papers.title: Exactness of colimits and amenability are independent for categories of finite substructures
papers.abstract: Let M be a countable homogeneous structure, G its automorphism group and A the category of its finite substructures and embeddings. The colimit functor on diagrams of R-modules indexed by A is exact if and only if the functor of coinvariants N ↦ N_G is exact on the R[G]-modules in which every element has an open stabilizer; this is a property of the topos of continuous G-sets. We compare it with amenability of G, the existence of invariant probability measures on compact spaces on which G acts, and show that neither implies the other. For the generic partially ordered set with an independent linear order, colimits are exact over every ring, while the group is not amenable by a result of Kechris and Sokić. For the vector space of countable dimension over the field with two elements, with a generic linear order on its non-zero vectors, the group is amenable and colimits are exact over the rational numbers, but they are exact over no ring in which 2 is not invertible. The first statement rests on a transfer theorem: if a subgroup H has exact coinvariants and finitely many orbits on each G/G_B, then exactness for G over a field k is equivalent to the existence of a G-invariant, finitely additive, k-valued function of total mass 1 on the expansions that H defines; positivity is not required. For posets this function has integer values, given by Euler characteristics of cells of order cones, which are values of the measure of Harman and Snowden for the automorphism group of the ordered real line. A consequence is that the separation property proved by Evans for Ramsey structures holds for a structure that is not a Ramsey structure but is obtained from one by forgetting a relation.

papers.title: Fast Queries of Fibered Barcodes
papers.abstract: The fibered barcode $\mathcal{F}(M)$ of a bipersistence module $M$ is the map sending each non-negatively sloped affine line $\ell \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ to the barcode of the restriction of $M$ along $\ell$. The simplicity, computability, and stability of $\mathcal{F}(M)$ make it a natural choice of invariant for data analysis applications. In an earlier preprint [arXiv:1512.00180], we introduced a framework for real-time interactive visualization of $\mathcal{F}(M)$, which allows the user to select a single line $\ell$ via a GUI and then plots the associated barcode. This visualization is a key feature of our software RIVET for the visualization and analysis of bipersistent homology. Such interactive visualization requires a framework for efficient queries of $\mathcal{F}(M)$, i.e., for quickly obtaining the barcode along a given line $\ell$. To enable such queries, we introduced a novel data structure based on planar line arrangements, called an augmented arrangement. The aim of the present paper is to give an updated and improved exposition of the parts of our preprint [arXiv:1512.00180] concerning the mathematics of the augmented arrangement and its computation. Notably, by taking the input to be a minimal presentation rather than a chain complex, we are able to substantially simplify our main algorithm and its complexity analysis.

papers.title: Finite graph certificates for composite terms in rational floor sequences
papers.abstract: For every real number \(\xi>0\), we give computer-assisted proofs that \(\lfloor\xi(7/5)^n\rfloor\) is divisible by at least one of \(2,3,5,11,13\) for infinitely many positive integers \(n\), and that \(\lfloor\xi(5/2)^n\rfloor\) is divisible by at least one of \(2,3,7,11,13,17,19,23,29,31\) for infinitely many positive integers \(n\), and that \(\lfloor\xi(5/3)^n\rfloor\) is divisible by at least one of \(2,3,7,11,13,17,19,23,29,31,37\) for infinitely many positive integers \(n\). Consequently all three sequences contain infinitely many composite terms. The proofs represent an orbit avoiding the given primes by a walk in a finite labelled graph whose vertices record residues and fractional cells and whose edges carry signed carries. Components whose output depends only on a cyclic phase are excluded by an elementary nonperiodicity lemma. In the word-labelled construction the edges carry finite carry words; deterministic paths are contracted exactly, and each new prime is imposed at every intermediate time of a word. For \(5/3\) chains of in-degree one are also contracted exactly, which keeps the largest graph at about \(2.1\cdot10^7\) vertices instead of about \(3.1\cdot10^8\). For the ratio \(7/5\) we also prove an explicit waiting-time bound: if \(P=\lfloor\xi\rfloor>13\) then some term with index at most \(428+12L(P)\), \(L(P)=\min\{h\ge0:5^h\ge P+2\}\), is divisible by one of the five primes. We then determine the reach of this certificate method: contraction, prime powers, and the primes dividing \(2ab\) do not enlarge the class of finitely certifiable bases; the method cannot terminate when \(a\ge2\operatorname{rad}M\); and the product \(R\) of the auxiliary primes not dividing \(2ab\) must satisfy \(a\le2R\,J(N_0)\) for the Jacobsthal function \(J\), whence \(R\ge a^{1-o(1)}\) by an elementary bound. The base \(5/3\) belongs to the finitely certifiable class, and no certificate of this kind for \(5/3\) uses only primes up to \(23\). Every adopted finite computation, including the certificate computation for \(5/3\), was performed by two implementations with disjoint scientific cores, which agree element by element on all compared finite data; the \(5/3\) obstruction witness is checked by one direct program. Lean proofs cover all three divisibility theorems and their compositeness corollaries: the one-step proof for \(7/5\) is kernel-checked, and the word-labelled proofs, including the one for \(5/3\), combine kernel-checked soundness theorems with native_decide finite evaluations, which add trust in the compiler and native evaluation.

papers.title: Finiteness and completeness of $g$-fans for real-weighted quivers
papers.abstract: We study finiteness and completeness of $g$-fans for quivers with positive real weights. We characterize finite Coxeter type by the condition that every weight in the mutation class has the form $2\cos(\pi/m)$ for some integer $m\geq3$. Under total sign-coherence, we then show that a quiver with finitely many $g$-clusters is $2$-finite, that is, every weight in its mutation class is less than $2$. This also gives a new proof that $g$-finiteness implies finite Coxeter type. Assuming in addition that, for every initial quiver in the mutation class, each $c$-vector on a coordinate axis is a signed standard basis vector, we prove that the $g$-fan is complete if and only if there are finitely many $g$-clusters. The main geometric result states that the coordinate projection of every $g$-cone is contained in a $g$-cone of the corresponding full subquiver. Consequently, completeness and density pass to full subquivers.

papers.title: Flexible algebraic curves and fake vanishing cycles
papers.abstract: We prove that complex curves in sufficiently ample linear systems on simply connected projective surfaces are topologically (spin) flexible: any (spin) mapping class of the underlying real surface extends to a topological mapping class of the ambient 4-manifold. As a corollary, we prove that smooth curves in the complex projective plane are topologically (spin) flexible. A consequence of topological flexibility is the existence of fake vanishing cycles, that is, simple closed curves on the underlying real surface that are not vanishing cycles, yet still bound a topologically embedded $(\pm1)$-framed disk in the surface exterior. We also give examples of pushed in Seifert surfaces in $D^4$ that are not topologically spin-flexible, but become spin-flexible after a single internal stabilization. Our methods utilize the equivariant intersection form on the surface exterior.

papers.title: Full Support For the Degree-Zero Hitchin Morphism
papers.abstract: We present a draft argument for the full-support conjecture for the canonical GLn Hitchin morphism in degree zero over a smooth complex projective curve of genus at least two. The whole-base Ng\^o support equality yields a finite necessary classification in terms of weighted products of maximal equigeneric spectral-factor families. We study their generic nodality, develop moving-cycle arguments for arbitrary multiplicities, and give an intersection calculation using generalized parabolic presentations and intrinsic Nash transforms. We relate the full-base Ng\^o string to the BPS formula for intersection Hodge numbers in every rank and give the genus-two rank-three Hodge table. The arguments developed here are presented for mathematical checking and revision by the authors. And the article is generated by ChatGPT, the author is trying his best to comprehense the article and the human's version is coming soon.

papers.title: Generalized Tate--Nakayama duality for complexes of tori over local function fields
papers.abstract: We define the cohomology set $H^{1}(\mathcal{E}, Z \to T \to U)$ for a complex $Z \to T \to U$ with $T$, $U$ tori over a local function field $F$ and $Z$ a finite subgroup of $T$, where $\mathcal{E}$ is the gerbe from [Dil23]. We follow the method of [Kal26] and prove that the Tate--Nakayama isomorphism [Dil23, Theorem 4.10] for $H^{1}(\mathcal{E}, Z \to T)$ extends to $H^{1}(\mathcal{E}, Z \to T \to U)$, which lets one generalize Kaletha's parametrization [Kal21] of supercuspidal $L$-packets to local function fields.

papers.title: Geometric Manin's Conjecture for Fano 3-Folds
papers.abstract: We classify families of free rational curves on all smooth Fano threefolds over the complex numbers. In particular, we prove the family of very free rational curves representing any fixed numerical curve class is either irreducible or empty. This proves Geometric Manin's Conjecture in dimension three. For general Fano threefolds of each deformation type, our results allow us to explicitly count the number of components of the moduli space of irreducible, geometrically rational curves, which may not be free, representing any numerical class.

papers.title: Gorenstein symmetry can fail for noetherian rings
papers.abstract: We construct a two-sided noetherian ring $A$ which has injective dimension $1$ as a left module over itself and infinite injective dimension as a right module over itself. This shows that Gorenstein symmetry can fail for two-sided noetherian rings. It is further shown that there is such an example over any field of characteristic different than $2$, that it has a dualizing complex, and that its derived category of right modules does not satisfy injective-generation in the sense of Rickard-Keller.

papers.title: Hecke Actions and Pure Inner Forms in Families of Real Langlands Parameters
papers.abstract: Let $H$ be a connected quasi-split real reductive group. We construct, on the stack of flagged Langlands parameters, a compact object for each pure inner form of $H$. Its finite Hecke translates generate a summand of the periodic coherent category. These summands are mutually orthogonal and exhaust the category over the entire marked Cartan. For each quasi-split form the corresponding summand is equivalent, as a finite Hecke module, to the periodic category of sheaves with nilpotent singular support on its enhanced real flag quotient. For a complex group regarded as real, the comparison is monoidal. For the full pure inner class we prove the equivalence on the open set where the roots taking value one span a space of rank at most one. It holds everywhere if each pure inner form is quasi-split or compact modulo its center. The comparisons preserve the marked parameter and the original boundary circle class. For every pure inner form we also compute the maps from an arbitrary standard Hecke translate to its closed generator. The nonzero terms are lines on a finite cover of the norm torus. Their shifts and both Cartan actions agree with those on the real flag variety.

papers.title: Heights and energies of polarized fibrations of varieties II. Fibrations over a polarized base
papers.abstract: We extend the height and energy inequalities for fibrations over curves to a fibration $f:X\to Y$ over a polarized variety $(Y,B)$. For an integrable relatively nef adelic line bundle $\bar L$, we prove a height inequality under the assumption that $L$ is nef on the inverse image of a geometric generic complete-intersection curve in $Y$. We deduce a lower bound for the local energy at almost every complex or nonarchimedean realization of a fixed polarized model when $L$ is $f$-ample. For a slope semistable bundle on a fixed polarized complex variety, we show that the infimum of the energy on its projective bundle equals the infimum of Donaldson's functional on Hermitian quotient metrics, with the normalization given below.

papers.title: Hilbert's Nullstellensatz is in AM from a zero-free half-plane of Dedekind zeta functions, after Koiran
papers.abstract: In 1996 Koiran proved, assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH), that deciding whether a system of polynomial equations with integer coefficients has a complex solution (Hilbert's Nullstellensatz, HN) is in the Arthur-Merlin class AM, hence in the second level of the polynomial hierarchy. GRH enters his proof through one estimate, a count of the primes modulo which an irreducible integer polynomial has a root. We show that this estimate, with exponent $7/8+\varepsilon$ in place of $1/2$, follows in two lines from the effective Chebotarev theorem in B. Hu's preprint on the zero-free half-plane $\Re s>7/8$, and that Koiran's proof then runs with primes of an explicit, polynomial bit length. Any zero-free half-plane $\Re s>\theta$, $\theta<1$, common to all Dedekind zeta functions suffices, for instance $\Re s>31/32$ of Cureton and Thorner: the estimate is then Frei, Sofos and Widmer's effective Chebotarev theorem, as Baldwin and Sivek used it for one polynomial in work on 3-manifold recognition, and the step to AM is Proposition 17.2 of our paper hexagon:2611.00987. So HN is in AM granted Hu's theorem or that of Cureton and Thorner. Both are unrefereed preprints of October 2026; the second is formalized in Lean according to its authors. Through published reductions that use GRH only via Koiran's theorem, the dimension problem and the parametric Nullstellensatz are then in AM, vanishing of Schubert coefficients is in AM $\cap$ coAM in types $A$-$D$, so it is not NP-hard unless the polynomial hierarchy collapses to its second level, and homogeneous systems of parameters are constructible in $\mathrm{FP}^{\Sigma_2^{\mathrm P}}$. Andrews, Garg and Schost placed HN in the counting hierarchy with no hypothesis; AM is the smaller class.
