papers.title: Homotopy types of complexes of hyperplanes in quasi-median graphs and applications to right-angled Artin groups
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove that, given two finite connected graphs $\Gamma_1$ and $\Gamma_2$, if the two right-angled Artin groups $A(\Gamma_1)$ and $A(\Gamma_2)$ are quasi-isometric, then the infinite pointed sums $\bigvee_\mathbb{N} \Gamma_1^{\bowtie}$ and $\bigvee_\mathbb{N} \Gamma_2^{\bowtie}$ are homotopy equivalent, where $\Gamma_i^{\bowtie}$ denotes the simplicial complex whose vertex-set is $\Gamma_i$ and whose simplices are given by joins. These invariants are extracted from a study, of independent interest, of the homotopy types of several complexes of hyperplanes in quasi-median graphs (such as one-skeleta of CAT(0) cube complexes). For instance, given a quasi-median graph $X$, the \emph{crossing complex} $\mathrm{Cross}^\triangle(X)$ is the simplicial complex whose vertices are the hyperplanes (or $\theta$-classes) of $X$ and whose simplices are collections of pairwise transverse hyperplanes. When $X$ has no cut-vertex, we show that $\mathrm{Cross}^\triangle(X)$ is homotopy equivalent to the pointed sum of the links of all the vertices in the prism-completion $X^\square$ of $X$.

papers.title: Infinite lower triangular matrices that are similar to their inverses but are not products of two involutions
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a field, and let $\GL_{\cf}(F)$ be the group of invertible column-finite matrices over $F$ indexed by $\bbN\times\bbN$. Denote by $\LT(F)$ (resp.\ $\UT(F)$) the subgroup consisting of lower (resp.\ upper) triangular matrices whose diagonal entries are equal to $1$. Every matrix in $\UT(F)$ is a product of two involutions. We show that, if $F$ has at least four elements, then $\LT(F)$ contains a matrix which is conjugate to its inverse by an invertible lower triangular matrix, but is not a product of two involutions in $\GL_{\cf}(F)$. The matrices can be chosen to be $4$-periodic. This gives a negative answer to a conjecture of de Seguins Pazzis.

papers.title: Infinitely many Wilson primes on the curves y^2 = x^p - x + a
papers.abstract: For an odd prime p and a nonzero a in F_p let A = F_p[x,y]/(y^2 - x^p + x - a), the coordinate ring of a curve of genus (p-1)/2 with one point at infinity. With the notion of Wilson prime of Hexagon 2611.01011, we prove: if P in F_p[y] is irreducible and P(y) is a prime element of A, then P(y) is a Wilson prime if and only if P'' = 0. We deduce that each of these rings has infinitely many Wilson primes, given explicitly: for p >= 5 the binomials y^t - c, with c a primitive root modulo p and t running through the powers of a suitable prime divisor of p-1 that are congruent to 1 modulo p. The proof rests on the criterion of Hexagon 2611.01011 and on the fact that, on any curve y^2 = f(x) in odd characteristic, the correction term of that criterion vanishes for the prime elements that are polynomials in y. The criterion is the exact analogue of Thakur's criterion for F_q[t].

papers.title: Integral Hodge/Tate conjecture of quotients via weak approximation
papers.abstract: For a finite group acting on a smooth projective separably rationally connected variety over an algebraically closed field, we prove that the rational quotient map induces a surjection from the coinvariants of its second Kato homology onto the second Kato homology of any smooth projective quotient model (with coefficients invertible in the ground field). The integral Hodge and Tate conjectures for one-cycles consequently descend to such quotient models. The proof uses weak approximation over function fields to retain the image of a smooth fiber in the total space.

papers.title: Irrationality and differential equations: the work of Calegari, Dimitrov, and Tang
papers.abstract: Beautiful recent work of Calegari, Dimitrov, and Tang has given new methods for proving irrationality of certain arithmetically interesting constants, notably $L(2, \chi_{-3})$, building on ideas of Siegel, Andr\'e, Bost-Charles, and others. This note is meant to explain some of this work for the 2027 JMM Current Events Bulletin, and to situate it in context of some results and conjectures in arithmetic and algebraic geometry.

papers.title: Kostant's tori in apposition: the Borel subgroups are opposite
papers.abstract: On 22 October 1969 Grothendieck wrote to Kostant about pairs of maximal tori $T$, $T'$ of a complex simple adjoint group in apposition, $T'$ being the centraliser of a cyclic element. Choosing Borel subgroups $B \supset T$ and $B' \supset T'$, he asked whether $B$ and $B'$ are always in general position. The answer is yes, in every type and for all $|W|$ Borel subgroups through $T'$: every one of them is opposite to $B$, and also to the opposite Borel subgroup $B^-$. The proof takes a few lines from two published facts: $\operatorname{Lie}T'$ contains an element of $f + \mathfrak b$ with $f$ a principal nilpotent of $\mathfrak b^-$ (Kostant), and a Borel subalgebra containing such an element is opposite to $\mathfrak b$ (an argument of Bălibanu's). We give it in full, self-contained. In type $A$ the element of $f+\mathfrak b$ is the inverse of the cyclic element, and the statement becomes the transversality of the flags stable under a cyclic weighted shift, which we prove directly and formalise in Lean 4 with Mathlib, together with the flag forms in types $B$, $C$ and in part $D$. A computation modulo primes checks types $B_2$ to $B_7$ independently. For Grothendieck's second question, on a distinguished conjugacy class of quadruples invariant under the exterior automorphisms, the answer is no in type $A_{2l}$, where the exterior automorphism fixes no class; in the other types we computed, a construction with the Coxeter plane gives a canonical pair of invariant classes, exchanged by the sign of $e_{-\theta}$. This second part is conditional on a description of $N(T)\cap N(T')$ that no specialist has checked.

papers.title: Koszul duality in exact categories
papers.abstract: In this paper we establish Koszul duality-type results in the setting of chain complexes in exact categories. In particular, we prove generalisations of Vallette's Koszul duality theorem and Koszul duality along the lines of Lurie and Pridham. We also prove a connective version. We conclude with some applications. These include our main example, the category of complete bornological spaces over a Banach field, as well as a sketch of deformation theory in formal geometry.

papers.title: Line bundles on regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a connected simply-connected simple algebraic group over $\mathbb{C}$ and $B$ be a Borel subgroup of $G$. Let $Y$ be an irreducible regular semisimple Hessenberg variety in $G/B$. In this article, we give a necessary and sufficient condition for the natural restriction map $\mathrm{res}: \mathrm{Pic}(G/B)\longrightarrow \mathrm{Pic}(Y)$ of Picard groups induced by the inclusion $Y\subseteq G/B$ to be an isomorphism.

papers.title: Linear rank-\(k\) nonincreasing and preserving maps
papers.abstract: We characterize the linear maps between rectangular matrix spaces that carry matrices of rank at most \(k\) to matrices of rank at most \(k\). Over every field, such a map has the form \(X\mapsto MXN\) or \(X\mapsto MX\T N\), or its entire image has upper rank at most \(k\). The proof uses polynomial functions on determinantal loci and extends Loewy's infinite-field theorem to all finite fields. Over fields with more than two elements, exact preservation of rank \(k\) implies rank-\(k\) nonincrease. Over \(\F_2\), for each \(k\ge2\), we construct a rank-\(k\) preserver that sends a rank-one matrix to a matrix of rank \(k+1\). For maps whose images have upper rank \(k\), three block rank equalities characterize exact preservation. Over \(\C\), we combine the Huang--Landsberg classification with a degree obstruction on \(\mathrm{PGL}_k\) to show that every primitive core of upper rank four arising from a rank-four preserver is, up to equivalence and transposition, a projected exterior-product space on \(\C^5\). If either source dimension exceeds five, every complex rank-four preserver is standard with full-rank factors or is a compression. A \(4\times5\) example attains the bound. The degree obstruction also shows that, over any algebraically closed field, every linear map \(\M_k\to\Alt_{k+1}\) sends some invertible matrix to a matrix of rank at most \(k-2\) when \(4\mid k\).

papers.title: Local Graph Limits Do Not Determine Normalized Adjacency Rank over $\mathbb F_2$
papers.abstract: We construct two sequences of finite simple bipartite graphs of maximum degree three with the same Benjamini--Schramm limit and different limiting normalized adjacency ranks over $\mathbb F_2$. This disproves the finite-field rank convergence conjecture of Ab\'ert and Szegedy in characteristic two. On these graph sequences, a fixed radius-one XOR rule applied to independent uniform vertex bits has different limiting output entropies per vertex. We also give two sequences of bounded-degree two-dimensional simplicial complexes with the same local limit and different limiting second Betti numbers per vertex over $\mathbb F_2$. For some absolute $\varepsilon>0$, estimating the rank over $\mathbb F_2$ of an $N\times N$ binary matrix to within $\varepsilon N$ requires $\Omega(N)$ row or column queries, even with at most three ones per row and column. For a bounded-degree two-dimensional complex on $M$ vertices, estimating the second Betti number over $\mathbb F_2$ to within $\varepsilon M$ requires $\Omega(M)$ queries, each of which returns all simplices containing a specified vertex. Both bounds hold for randomized adaptive algorithms that succeed with probability at least $2/3$ on every input.

papers.title: Modular Schur functions and Macdonald characters
papers.abstract: Modular Schur functions arose from the problem of determining the characters of simple polynomial representations of the general linear group in positive characteristic. We prove three results about these functions. (i) In finitely many variables, we obtain two bases for a space of symmetric polynomials with bounded degree in each variable, one consisting of modular Schur polynomials and the other of products of truncated complete symmetric polynomials. (ii) We determine the signs of the nonzero Schur coefficients of modular Schur functions, show that their absolute values are at most the factorial of the block weight, and characterize equality. (iii) Over an infinite field of prime characteristic, a modular Schur polynomial is a simple polynomial character exactly when its indexing partition satisfies the Carter condition, provided the number of variables is at least the degree. Thus we prove three conjectures formulated by Walker (1994). We also use the Heisenberg operators from the Schur coefficient calculation to prove positivity for Macdonald characters. After centering the Macdonald parameters at one and negating the auxiliary variables, the normalized power-sum matrix entries of the Macdonald creation operator have nonnegative integer coefficients, which yields nonnegative rational coefficients for normalized Macdonald characters. The result for the creation operator confirms a conjecture of Ben Dali and D'Adderio (2024).

papers.title: Non-effective finite equivalence relations on finite schemes over a field: Venken's example checked, and a second one
papers.abstract: In 1961 Grothendieck asked whether a closed equivalence relation on a finite scheme over a field, with finite but not necessarily flat projections, is always effective. In a lecture at Buffalo in 1973 he still called the question open. It had been answered in the negative in 1971 by Venken, in a two-page note about the descent of flat modules whose Corollary 3.1 is a non-effective equivalence relation on the spectrum of a local Artin algebra of dimension $33$ in six variables, over any field. We give a second example, in two variables, of length $15$ ($16$ in characteristic $2$), obtained by restricting Raicu's non-effective relation on the affine plane to a finite subscheme cut out by squares of invariant functions. It is proved by hand, in every characteristic at once: a general lemma reduces the comparison of the two ideals in degree $5$ to the subalgebra $C$ generated by three invariant functions, and a linear form on the degree-$5$ part of $A \otimes_C A$ separates the obstruction. The example is shorter than Venken's; no minimality is claimed. We then recheck Venken's example by linear algebra, where the ideal of his relation exceeds, by one dimension in degree $4$, the ideal of $X \times_Y X$, $Y$ the quotient; this check is formalised in Lean, over any nonzero commutative ring, except for the dimension counts. The computer checks of both examples, over $\mathbb{Q}$ and over the finite prime fields that the pivots require, are reported separately from the proofs.

papers.title: Non-vanishing of the structure-sheaf cohomology of affine henselian schemes and henselian affinoids
papers.abstract: Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair such that $A$ is a domain of characteristic zero and $I\ne0$. We prove that any flat affine henselian scheme of finite presentation over $(A,I)$ has nonzero first structure-sheaf cohomology whenever one of its fibers over a point in $V(I)$ has positive dimension. This in particular gives a negative answer to the question by Devadas in the mixed-characteristic case. As an application, we also prove that the first structure-sheaf cohomology does not vanish for henselian affinoids of positive dimensions.

papers.title: On the action of the mapping class group on the fundamental group of a surface
papers.abstract: We describe the action of the mapping class group $M(g,n)$ on the fundamental group of $S_{g,n}$, the complement of $n$ distinct points in a compact orientable surface of positive genus $g$. This is achieved by computing the image of the generators of $M(g,n)$ as outer automorphisms of the fundamental group.

papers.title: On the generalized foliated cone theorem of rank one
papers.abstract: We prove the cone theorem for generalized foliated quadruples of rank one in arbitrary dimension. As an application, we prove the uniqueness of MMP outputs for log canonical generalized foliated quadruples of rank one.

papers.title: On the Hernandez–Leclerc formula
papers.abstract: We prove the Hernandez–Leclerc geometric $q$-character formula for every real simple module in $\mathcal C^-$, in all finite Dynkin types and at every $q\in\mathbb C^\times$ that is not a root of unity. The coefficients are ordinary Euler characteristics of quiver Grassmannians of the prescribed generic injective kernel.

papers.title: On the leading constant in Manin's conjecture
papers.abstract: We disprove a conjecture of Batyrev and Tschinkel concerning counting rational points of bounded height. Our results strongly suggest that the transcendental Brauer group plays a role in the leading constant in problems of the same nature such as the Manin--Peyre conjecture.

papers.title: On the unirationality of anticanonical weighted complete intersection surfaces: the infinite families
papers.abstract: Anticanonical weighted complete intersection surfaces fall into finitely many sporadic families and four infinite families. We prove that the anticanonical surfaces lying in the infinite families are unirational over their field of definition. Over a Hilbertian field, we further prove that a Hilbert subset of members consists of nonrational surfaces.

papers.title: Orbit closures of generic rational polygons with at least five sides
papers.abstract: Mirzakhani and Wright attach to the angles $\theta$ of a rational polygon the orbit closure $\mathcal M(\theta)$ of the unfolding of almost every polygon with these angles. They ask whether, for more than four sides, $\mathcal M(\theta)$ can be anything other than a connected component of a stratum of Abelian differentials or a locus of double covers of a component of a stratum of quadratic differentials. It cannot. For every choice of five or more angles, $\mathcal M(\theta)$ is the component of its stratum if the least common denominator $k$ of the angles divided by $\pi$ is odd, and the locus of holonomy double covers of the component of its quadratic stratum if $k$ is even. When some $s$ of the angles sum to $(s-1)\pi$, Apisa and Aygun treat this case by a different method; our proof does not depend on theirs. We read the rank of $\mathcal M(\theta)$ off characters of the deck rotation of the unfolding and induct on the number of sides by colliding two vertices; where no collision applies, arithmetic modulo $k$ takes its place. We also extend Mirzakhani and Wright's nonvanishing of the second fundamental form from triangles to every number of sides.

papers.title: Orbit closures of generic rational quadrilaterals
papers.abstract: Delecroix and Rüth conjectured that their lists of admissible and reduced rational triangle and quadrilateral types whose unfoldings do not have dense orbits in their ambient strata are complete, and they proved this for quadrilaterals with angles $2\pi a_i/N$ when $N\le32$. We prove the conjecture for quadrilaterals, for the generic quadrilateral with given angles. For every admissible and reduced type outside their seven quadrilateral exceptions, the orbit closure of the unfolding of the generic member is a connected component of a stratum of Abelian differentials if $N$ is odd or $N\equiv2\pmod4$, and the locus of holonomy double covers of a component of a stratum of quadratic differentials if $4$ divides $N$. The proof reads the rank of the orbit closure off a set of characters of the deck rotation of the unfolding, a cyclic cover of the sphere. Mirzakhani and Wright's rules, as extended for triangles in the two earlier papers of this series, constrain this set, and two further inputs bring in the orbit closures of triangles: the collision of two vertices, through Mirzakhani and Wright's boundary theorem, and symmetric members of the family of cyclic covers, which cover unfoldings of triangles. Parts of the proof, including a census up to $N=1000$, are computer-assisted.

papers.title: Orbit closures of scalene rational triangles: every denominator
papers.abstract: Delecroix and Rüth conjectured that, apart from an explicit list, the unfoldings of rational triangles and quadrilaterals without a reflection symmetry have dense $\mathrm{GL}(2,\mathbb{R})$-orbits in their ambient strata, and proved this for the triangles with angles $p_i\pi/N$ and $N\le58$. We prove the conjecture for triangles. If a scalene rational triangle is not on their list of three infinite families and nine triangles, the orbit closure of its unfolding is the connected component of its stratum when $N$ is odd, and the locus of holonomy double covers of a connected component of a stratum of quadratic differentials when $N$ is even. With the first paper of this series, it follows that the orbit is not dense in that locus for the triangles on the list, except possibly for the triangle with angles $(3\pi/20,\pi/5,13\pi/20)$. Most of the proof concerns subgroups of the units modulo $N$; parts of it, including all of $N\le58$, are computer-assisted.

papers.title: Orbit closures of scalene rational triangles: rank one and prime denominators
papers.abstract: The unfolding of a rational triangle is a translation surface, and the closure of its $\mathrm{GL}(2,\mathbb{R})$-orbit has a rank, which is one for lattice surfaces. We determine the scalene rational triangles of rank one: besides the known lattice triangles, which form three infinite families and four further triangles, they are the two triangles found by Delecroix and Rüth's computer search, with angles $(\pi/10,3\pi/10,3\pi/5)$ and $(\pi/12,\pi/4,2\pi/3)$, whose unfoldings are Prym eigenforms. We also prove that for a scalene triangle with angles $p_i\pi/N$, $N$ prime, the orbit closure of the unfolding is a connected component of its stratum. Delecroix and Rüth conjectured that the scalene triangles whose unfoldings do not have dense orbits in their ambient strata form an explicit list. The second theorem proves this for prime denominators, and by the first, every scalene triangle of rank one whose unfolding does not have a dense orbit in its ambient stratum is on their list. The proofs differentiate the holomorphic eigenforms of the unfolding's rotational symmetry along every direction of the orbit closure; at a prime denominator this leaves a statement about subgroups of the units modulo $N$, proved with character sums, a count of lattice points and a computation.

papers.title: Parke-Taylor Varieties
papers.abstract: Parke--Taylor functions are certain rational functions on the Grassmannian of lines encoding MHV amplitudes in particle physics. For $n$ particles there are $n!$ Parke--Taylor functions, corresponding to all orderings of the particles. Linear relations between these functions have been extensively studied in the last years. We here describe all non-linear polynomial relations between these functions in a simple combinatorial way and study the variety parametrized by them, called the Parke--Taylor variety. We show that the Parke--Taylor variety is equal to the log canonical embedding of the moduli space $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$ into $\mathbb{P}^{(n-2)!-1}$ due to Keel and Tevelev by exhibiting a concrete linear isomorphism with the realization in coordinates based on Kapranov's map. We also show that the intersection with the algebraic torus recovers the open part, $\mathcal{M}_{0,n}$. We give an explicit description of this isomorphism. Unlike the realization of the log canonical embedding by using the iterated Kapranov's map, this Parke--Taylor embedding very explicitly respects the symmetry of the $n$ marked points and is constructed in a single-step procedure, avoiding the intermediate embedding into a product of projective spaces.

papers.title: Partition growth homomorphisms on Specht modules
papers.abstract:
There is a unique (up to scalar) representation homomorphism between the Specht modules $\mathcal{S}^\lambda$ and $\mathcal{S}^\mu$ when $\mu$ is obtained from $\lambda$ by adding one to a part of $\lambda$. We find explicit formulas for these homomorphisms in the Specht polynomial bases of $\mathcal{S}^\lambda$ and $\mathcal{S}^\mu$. Furthermore, given two representation homomorphisms corresponding to adding one to two different parts of $\lambda$, we find the commutator for the composition of these two homomorphisms.
  We also extend the Specht polynomial basis of $\mathcal{S}^\lambda$ into a basis of the permutation module $\mathcal{H}^\lambda$ and explicitly find a formula for the skew isomorphism from $\mathcal{S}^\lambda$ to $\mathcal{S}^{\lambda'}$.

papers.title: Positive Geometry of Oriented Matroid Strata
papers.abstract: We study the positive geometry of Grassmannians whose boundary is a union of Pl\"ucker divisors. For the full Pl\"ucker boundary the regions are closures of realization spaces of uniform oriented matroids. In rank three we show that the pair $(\mathrm{Gr}_{3,n},Z_{3,n})$ is a positive arrangement in the sense of Sturmfels and Telen for $n\le 9$ points and compute its combinatorial rank from point counts of the configuration space $\mathcal{X}_{3,n}$ over finite fields. For seven points the canonical forms of the regions span all logarithmic forms. For eight points they do not, because the M\"obius-Kantor configuration is not realizable over the reals. This determines for seven and eight points whether the integrands of Cachazo, Early and Zhang for the generalized biadjoint amplitudes of Cachazo, Early, Guevara and Mizera span the space of logarithmic forms. From ten points on, the genus is positive because a K3 surface appears in the boundary. For smaller boundaries and arbitrary rank we give a recursion that adds one point at a time and preserves the genus and the combinatorial rank. It recovers the positive Grassmannian and shows that realization spaces of stacked polytopes are regions of positive arrangements of combinatorial rank one.

papers.title: Prescribed oscillating spectra and isomorphism types in $C[0,1]$
papers.abstract: The oscillating spectrum of a closed subspace of $C[0,1]$ is the set of points at which its unit ball fails to be equicontinuous. Given nonempty $F_\sigma$ sets $A,B\subseteq[0,1]$, we prove that every closed subspace with spectrum $A$ is nonisomorphic to every closed subspace with spectrum $B$ if and only if one set is countable and the other is nonmeager. We show that a countable spectrum forces the dual to be separable, while a nonmeager spectrum forces the dual to be nonseparable. For every uncountable meager $F_\sigma$ set $M$ and every separable infinite-dimensional real Banach space $E$, we construct an isomorphic copy of $E$ in $C[0,1]$ with spectrum $M$. We also show that every nonempty $F_\sigma$ set admits an uncomplemented realization. For a prescribed nonempty finite spectrum, we show that an infinite-dimensional Banach space admits a realization precisely when it embeds isomorphically into $c_0$. Using the Schreier family, we construct a norm-one complemented subspace of $C[0,1]$ with compact countably infinite spectrum that does not embed isomorphically into $c_0$. This example and the classification of pairs answer Questions~4.3 and~4.9, respectively, of Enflo, Gurariy, and Seoane-Sep\'ulveda.

papers.title: Progress on the Stable Fields Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove that every infinite stable field of positive characteristic is separably closed. We also show that the field $\mathbb{C}(t)$ has the strict order property (hence is unstable).

papers.title: Quantum Adams operations in quasimap K-theory
papers.abstract: We define quantum deformations of Adams operations in $K$-theory, in the framework of quasimap quantum $K$-theory. They provide $K$-theoretic analogs of the quantum Steenrod operations from equivariant symplectic Gromov--Witten theory. We verify the compatibility of these operations with the Kahler and equivariant $q$-difference module structures, provide sample computations via $\mathbb{Z}/k$-equivariant localization, and identify them with $p$-curvature operators of the Kahler $q$-difference connections as studied in Koroteev-Smirnov. We also formulate and verify a $K$-theoretic quantum Hikita conjecture at roots of unity, and propose an indirect algebro-geometric definition of quantum Steenrod operations.

papers.title: Quasifibrations in \'etale homotopy theory
papers.abstract:
We study quasifibrations in \'etale homotopy theory and prove a criterion for a morphism of schemes to be a quasifibration in terms of its (higher) direct images for sheaves of sets and (possibly non-abelian) groups. This allows to generalise Friedlander's formula for the homotopy fibre of geometric fibrations to the case of an arbitrary qcqs base scheme that is not necessarily normal.
  Among the applications to geometric fibrations are (1) specialisation is an equivalence on the pro-$\Sigma$ completed profinite \'etale homotopy types of geometric fibres, (2) a long exact sequence of \'etale homotopy groups in characteristic 0, and (3) a partially $\Sigma$-completed exact sequence of \'etale homotopy groups in low degree terms in general.

papers.title: Rank Recursion for $q$-Whittaker and Macdonald Operators
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce and prove a set of rank recurrence relations for $q$-Whittaker and Macdonald operators. We also derive an explicit expression for the $k$-th power of the $q$-Whittaker operators in terms of the $q$-deformed binomial probability distribution, and we express the rank recurrence relations for the Macdonald operators in terms of the Cauchy determinant.

papers.title: Resurgence of the squeezed Kerr oscillator: tunnel splittings, Kummer connection, and a perturbative/non-perturbative relation
papers.abstract: The squeezed (two-photon-driven) Kerr oscillator $H=a^{\dagger2}a^2-\epsilon_2(a^{\dagger2}+a^2)-\Delta a^\dagger a$, in units of the Kerr constant, underlies the Kerr-cat qubit. Its two wells at $a=\pm\alpha$, $\alpha^2=\epsilon_2+\Delta/2$, carry doublets of nearly degenerate cat states. We give the resurgent structure of these doublets at fixed detuning $\Delta$ as $\epsilon_2\to\infty$. The splitting of the $n$th doublet is \[ E_{\mathrm{odd},n}-E_{\mathrm{even},n}=\frac{8\epsilon_2(4\epsilon_2)^{2n-\Delta/2}\,\ee^{-2\epsilon_2}}{n!\,\Gamma(n-\Delta/2)}\,\big(1+O(\epsilon_2^{-1})\big). \] In the Bargmann representation, the factor $1/\Gamma(n-\Delta/2)$ is a Kummer connection coefficient, and its zeros are the known exact degeneracies at $\Delta=2m\ge 2n$. At fixed $\Delta$ and leading order, the known large-detuning WKB formula is the same expression with $\Gamma(1+\Delta/2)$ replaced by its Stirling approximation. The Rayleigh--Schr\"odinger series of each level in $1/\alpha^2$, computed exactly through order $150$, diverges as $\Gamma(j+4n-\Delta)4^{-j}$ with the prefactor fixed by the splitting, and converges at $\Delta=2$ for $n=0$. The median Borel sum of the $n=0$ series reproduces the center of the exact ground doublet up to a real two-instanton term, which a quantization condition obtained from the same matching predicts at leading order. Finally, the corrections $1+k_1/\epsilon_2+k_2/\epsilon_2^2+\cdots$ to the splitting obey a relation of Dunne--\"Unsal type with the perturbative energies: the predicted closed forms---for $k_1$ in $n$ and $\Delta$ (checked for $n\le2$ and at $(n,\Delta)=(3,2)$), $k_2$ (checked for $n\le2$), and $k_3$ (checked for $n=0$)---agree with the values extracted from exact splittings, including $k_2$ for $n=2$ and $k_3$ for $n=0$, which were not used to find the relation. With three correction terms, the formula agrees with exact diagonalization to a relative error below $2\times10^{-5}$ for $-1\le\Delta\le3$ at $\epsilon_2\ge10$ (including the limit at the exact zeros), and below $2\times10^{-4}$ for $-1\le\Delta\le11$ at $\epsilon_2=30$.

papers.title: RSK with a twist, mirabolic Steinberg variety, and Pak--Postnikov representations
papers.abstract: There is a beautiful interplay between the classical Robinson--Schensted correspondence and the Steinberg variety, which is the union of conormal components of $Fl(V) \times Fl(V)$. The irreducible components of the Steinberg variety gives the geometric interpretation of RS, and Pak--Postnikov description of RS as U,D operators is the combinatorics shadow of the $S_n\times S_n$-representation inside the top homology of the Steinberg variety. We study the conormal components of $Fl(V) \times Fl(V) \times L(\lambda)$, where $L(\lambda)$ is an irreducible representation of $GL(V)$. We show that there are only three families of $L(\lambda)$ such that $Fl(V)\times Fl(V) \times L(\lambda)$ has finitely many orbits. These families are determinant twists of classical RS, Travkin's mirabolic RSK and its Fourier dual. We extend the combinatorial interpretation of RS in terms of U,D operators to mirabolic RSK. Finally, we give a filtration of the top homology of the mirabolic Steinberg variety in which each graded piece is a Pak--Postnikov $S_n \times S_n$-representations.

papers.title: Schubert positivity for filtered bundles
papers.abstract: We characterize formal filtered nefness of a formal quotient flag on a polarized Hodge--Lefschetz module by the formal nefness of its positive-rank total quotients. Using this criterion, we prove that quotient Schubert functors preserve formal nefness and that Schubert incidence modules inherit every commuting formally filtered nef flag. As geometric and numerical consequences, we recover the positivity criteria of Fulton--Lazarsfeld and Fulton and extend the Lorentzian polynomial theorem of Lu and Zheng to derived Schubert classes of filtered bundles. In combinatorics, our framework applies to tautological flags of flag matroids on ordinary and augmented matroid Chow rings as well as on the intersection cohomology of rational projective fans equipped with a common weight map. We deduce concordance-sensitive intersection inequalities, establish the Schubert positivity of the leading Riemann--Roch Chow class of a flag matroid, and show that the nonvanishing supports of derived Schubert numbers on an augmented Chow ring form the Higgs lifts of an intrinsically determined matroid quotient.

papers.title: Semi-local Zariski-van Kampen theorems
papers.abstract: Zariski-van Kampen theorems are meant to constitute a complement to Lefschetz-Zariski theorems which, in turn, generalize the classical Lefschetz theorem on hyperplane sections to quasi-projective varieties or to the corresponding local case. Semi-local Zariski-van Kampen theorems are developed here as a tool which is useful both in the local and in the global case.

papers.title: Simultaneous Waring problems for binary forms and the geometry of rational curves
papers.abstract:
We investigate the simultaneous Waring problem for binary forms and its geometric applications to rational curves. By analyzing the minimal free resolution of the simultaneous annihilator, we establish formulas for both simultaneous Waring ranks and border Waring ranks including explicit computations for binary monomials.
  As a geometric application, we explicitly describe parametrizations of rational curves up to projective equivalence. We determine the minimum dimension of a rational normal scroll containing the curve as a section of its ruling in terms of the minimal generators of the corresponding simultaneous annihilator. For rational curves lying as divisors on rational normal surface scrolls, we characterize their smoothness and describe the generators of their defining ideals.

papers.title: Single-valued flat connections in several variables on arbitrary Riemann surfaces
papers.abstract: Polylogarithms on Riemann surfaces may be constructed systematically in terms of flat connections that can enjoy various algebraic and analytic properties. In this paper, we present a single-valued and modular invariant connection ${\cal J}_\text{DHS}$ on the configuration space $\text{Cf}_n(\Sigma)$ of an arbitrary number $n$ of points on an arbitrary compact Riemann surface $\Sigma$ with or without punctures. The connection ${\cal J}_\text{DHS}$ generalizes an earlier construction for a single variable and is built out of the same integration kernels. We show that ${\cal J}_\text{DHS}$ is flat on $\text{Cf}_n(\Sigma)$. For the case without punctures, we relate it to the meromorphic multiple-valued Enriquez connection ${\cal K}_\text{E}$ in $n$ variables on the universal cover $\tilde \Sigma$ of $\Sigma$ by the composition of a gauge transformation and an automorphism of the Lie algebra in which ${\cal J}_\text{DHS}$ and ${\cal K}_\text{E}$ take values. In a companion paper, we shall establish the equivalence between the flatness of these connections and the corresponding interchange and Fay identities, for arbitrary compact Riemann surfaces.

papers.title: Smooth convergents and the size of the next denominator
papers.abstract: Suppose an irrational $\xi$ has infinitely many continued-fraction convergents $P/q$ for which $|P|$, $q$, and the next denominator $Q$ have all their prime factors in a fixed finite set $S$. Marques proved that $\log Q\gg q^c$ at those indices for some $c>0$. When $S$ consists of two primes, the bound holds with $c=1$, which is sharp. When $S$ consists of three primes, the supremal exponent is at most $1/2$. In every fixed open subinterval of $(1,2)$, the minimum of $\log Q$ over $\xi$ and $P/q$ in the interval has order $\sqrt q$ at infinitely many powers $q$ of each prime in $S$. Let $N_q$ be the least $S$-smooth integer greater than $1$ congruent to $\pm1\pmod q$. For each $S$ with at least three primes, a single irrational realizes $P Q=N_q$ infinitely often.

papers.title: Stacks of Parabolic Vector Bundles in the Geometric Langlands Program
papers.abstract: I define a locus inside stacks of parabolic vector bundles on smooth projective curves which is important for the construction of twisted Hecke eigensheaves in the ramified geometric Langlands program for $\mathrm{GL}_n$. I give an explicit description of this locus in the case of rank $3$ parabolic vector bundles on $\mathbb{P}^1$ with parabolic structure at four points. This example involves partial flags in the level structure as well as a non-trivial twisted equivariance condition.

papers.title: Steiner porism and boundary value problems
papers.abstract:
The aim of this paper is to describe several interpretations of Steiner chains of circles in terms of certain boundary value problems and give a short review of related results. Our approach and discussion are motivated by the recent results on the geometry of Steiner porism based on an apparently novel analytic parametrization of poristic circles obtained by A.Diakvnishvili and the present author. We also mention a few feasible problems and generalizations suggested by the constructions and considerations presented in the paper.
  Keywords: Steiner chain of circles, Steiner porism, curvature, invariant moments of curvatures, boundary value problem, Riemann-Hilbert problem, Brylinski loop space, circle packing

papers.title: Supercuspidal representations and types via double covers and the Fourier--Weil representation
papers.abstract: We present a construction of supercuspidal representations and types for tame $p$-adic groups whose input is a generic essentially depth-zero representation of a double covers of twisted Levi subgroups. This clarifies and simplifies existing constructions by automatically producing and explaining the twisting quadratic character of Fintzen--Kaletha--Spice, the roots of unity in the Harish-Chandra character formula, and making the connection to the Galois side of the local Langlands correspondence immediate. The main innovation is the use of a Fourier model of the Weil representation defined on an extension of the symplectic group by the Witt group.

papers.title: Syzygies of general projections of canonical and paracanonical curves
papers.abstract:
Let $X\subset\mathbb{P}^r$ be an integral linearly normal variety and $R=k[x_0,\cdots,x_r]$ the coordinate ring of $\mathbb{P}^r$. It is known that the syzygies of $X$ contain some geometric information. In recent years the syzygies of non-projectively normal varieties or in other words, the projection $X'$ of $X$ away from a linear subspace $W\subset\mathbb{P}^r$, were taken into considerations. Assuming that the coordinate ring of the ambient space that $X'$ lives in is $S$, there are two types of vanishing properties of the Betti diagrams of the projected varieties, the so-called $N_{d,p}^S$ and $\widetilde{N}_{d,p}$. The former one have been widely discussed for general varieties, for example by S. Kwak, Y. Choi and E. Park, while the latter one was discussed by W. Lee and E. Park for curves of very large degree.
  In this paper I will discuss about the $\widetilde{N}_{d,p}$ properties of the projection of a generic canonical and paracanonical curve away from a generic point and in particular whether they are cut out by quadrics. Some conjectures will be claimed based on the tests on Macaulay2.

papers.title: Tensor powers of the Steinberg character of $GL_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$, zonotopal algebras, and quiver varieties
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the $m$-th tensor power ${\rm St}^{\otimes m}$ of the Steinberg character of $GL_n(q)$. To do that we use the connection between tensor products of unipotent characters and the cohomology of certain quiver varieties for star-shaped quivers \cite{L2}\cite{LRV}. We prove that the cohomology ring of the quiver variety associated to ${\rm St}^{\otimes m}$ is generated by its tautological classes. We use this to prove that this cohomology ring is isomorphic to a central zonotopal algebra. We then deduce a combinatorial formula for the multiplicities of unipotent characters in ${\rm St}^{\otimes m}$. This formula has been conjectured by the second author when $m=2$.

papers.title: The constant term in Cramer's mean-square theorem for the primes. Second-order asymptotics and limiting fluctuations of the prime energy
papers.abstract: Let $I(X)=\int_1^X(\psi(x)-x)^2x^{-2}\,dx$ be the energy of the primes. Under the Riemann hypothesis (RH) and simple zeros its slope is $C_B=2+\gamma_E-\log4\pi$ (Cram\'er). We study the next terms. Under RH, simple zeros and an additional spacing condition (H$^*$), $I(X)=C_B\log X+K+\Phi(\log X)+O(X^{-1/2})$, where $\Phi$ is an absolutely convergent almost periodic sum over pairs of zeros. The constant has a closed form without zeros, $K=\frac12C_B^2-C_B-\sigma_2+2(1+\gamma_E)\log2\pi-(\log4\pi-1)^2-1+2\sum_n\Lambda(n)\varphi(1/n)$, with $\sigma_2=\sum_\rho\rho^{-2}$ and $\varphi(y)=y-\operatorname{artanh}y-\frac y2\log(1-y^2)$; under RH, $K=2.512479790006\ldots$, certified to $6\cdot10^{-13}$ in interval arithmetic. Under RH and simple zeros alone, $K$ is the Ces\`aro mean in $\log X$ of $I(X)-C_B\log X$ if and only if $\sum_{0<|\gamma-\gamma'|<\varepsilon}|\rho\rho'|^{-1}=o(\varepsilon)$: a pair of zeros at distance $\lambda$ acts like a double zero for $\log X\ll1/\lambda$. Under (H$^*$), $I(X)-C_B\log X$ has a limiting logarithmic distribution with mean $K$ and variance $V$, an explicit double sum over zeros under linear independence, whose factors we check on finite sets of zeros; numerically $V=1.2502\cdot10^{-5}$ under LI. The primes up to $10^9$ agree with the zero side to $1.3\cdot10^{-5}$ (r.m.s.) and give $K=2.512484$. In the random models of the primes and of $\mu$ that we examine the median energy is $8$ to $150$ times larger. A Gaussian-window identity isolates the principal mode of each zero in the prime signal: a closed ellipse on the line, an expanding spiral off it. A final section assembles the slope, the intercept and the oscillation as one calibrated instrument, the energy gauge, with a multiplicity-meter reading of the slope and a ledger reading of the intercept, and runs it on the primes to $10^8$ beside $38$ zeros computed from scratch.

papers.title: The coordinate ring of the universal centralizer via Demazure operators
papers.abstract: We give a simple description of the coordinate ring of the universal centralizer associated to a simply connected semisimple group. To this end, we prove a general result on Weil restriction of affine schemes $X$ over the Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak{t}$ equipped with a compatible action of the Weyl group $W$. Specifically, we show that the coordinate ring of the scheme $\mathrm{Res}^W(X)$ of $W$-fixed points of Weil restriction of $X$ to the categorical quotient $\mathfrak{t}//W$ can be obtained from the coordinate ring of $X$ by applying Demazure operators if and only if the scheme $\mathrm{Res}^W(X)$ is integral.

papers.title: The divisor cross-energy has all its zeros on the critical line. Genealogy of the zeros of the reflected cross-energy and the Epstein control
papers.abstract: Cut by divisors, the reflected cross-energy of the Riemann zeta function has all its zeros on the critical line. For every $m$, with $M=m\,\mathrm{rad}(m)$, the divisor cross-energy $D_m(s)=M^{s-1}\sigma_{-s}(m)+M^{-s}\sigma_{s-1}(m)$ has all its zeros on $\re s=\frac12$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:divisor}). The Euler product factorizes the cut over the primes, and the Enestr\"om--Kakeya theorem, applied prime by prime, gives $|E_m(s)|>|E_m(1-s)|$ for $\re s>\frac12$; the ratio $\sqrt p$ between consecutive coefficients is what places the line at $\frac12$. With the coefficients of the Epstein zeta function of $x^2+5y^2$ on the same divisors (pole, functional equation, nonnegative coefficients, no Euler product) there are $12$ zeros off the line. The cut by size behaves differently. The reflected cross-energy $\CFR(N,s)=N^{-s}X_{N-1}(1-s)+N^{s-1}X_{N-1}(s)$, $X_N(s)=\sum_{n\le N}n^{-s}$, is a finite sum of hyperbolic cosines with positive coefficients, and for $N=2$ all its zeros lie on the critical line. As $N$ grows, zeros leave the line. For $\zeta$ they are transient: they sit at the heights of the zeros of $\zeta$ and their distance to the line decays like $1.1/\sqrt N$ ($0.144$ at $N\approx40$, $0.033$ at $N=1200$). For the Davenport--Heilbronn function the same construction keeps a permanent zero at $0.81+85.70i$, and for the Epstein function it keeps permanent zeros near $\sigma=0.9$. The passage from the divisor cut to the size cut is the convergence of partial Euler products in the strip, which is known to be equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis. The translation law at the zeros, $\lambda_\rho X_n(\rho)X_n(1-\rho)=n+\frac12+\frac{\lambda_\rho}{12n}+O(n^{-2})$ with $\lambda_\rho=\rho(1-\rho)$, holds for every zero on or off the line, and the Epstein function realizes it with a complex slope: pole, functional equation, positivity and the translation law are compatible with zeros off the line. We add three tools: the exact recursion $E_{N+1}=(\frac{N+1}N)^{s-1}(E_N+\frac1N)$ of the Hermite--Biehler pair; a ladder that brackets each zero from the previous ones, $R_k^{-1/k}\le\lambda_{n+1}\le R_k/R_{k+1}$; and the correction of the harmonic-function criterion of \cite{Ca17}, whose limit is $\frac1{2\lambda}$ and not $0$, which moves its zero-finding algorithm from $25.0083$, $30.4356$ to $25.0109$, $30.4248$ (true $25.010858$, $30.424876$). We also write the logarithm of the symmetrized Euler product as a cross-energy over the primes, $\sum_p2p^{-1/2}\cosh((s-\frac12)\log p)$, and locate its singularities on a ladder of lines $\re s=\frac1{2k},1-\frac1{2k}$. Finally, the arithmetic part of $\CFR$ is $\zeta(s)$ times an explicit nonvanishing factor, so $\CFR$ decides the Riemann hypothesis only through a Tur\'an-type criterion for a finite sum $T_N$, whose zeros, unlike those of the partial sums, stay out of $\sigma>\frac12$ up to $t\approx3$--$6N$; and $\zeta(s)=\frac12s(s+1)(J(s)-\frac1{\lambda_s})$ with $J$ the Mellin transform of the positive weight $\{x\}(1-\{x\})$, so that the zeros are the points where $J=1/\lambda$.

papers.title: The Lafforgue Transform
papers.abstract: In this report, we survey the \emph{Lafforgue transform}, a natural representation-theoretic map from the Kazhdan cocenter to the Bernstein center of a reductive group over a local field. Its motivation comes from our study of the Braverman-Kazhdan proposal, a conjectural framework for establishing the meromorphic continuation and functional equations of general automorphic $L$-functions through harmonic analysis on possibly singular varieties. For $G=\SL_2$ and $\GL_2$, we explain how the stable part of the Lafforgue transform and its distinguished section are realized as integral transforms on the Steinberg-Hitchin base, with formulas of motivic nature that are valid over every local field.

papers.title: The local intertwining relation for inner forms of $\mathrm{GL}_N$
papers.abstract: The local intertwining relation for inner forms of general linear groups over a local field asserts that the normalized intertwining operator for every parabolically induced representation arising from a local A-parameter is the identity operator. Our main theorem verifies the claim over local fields of characteristic zero. This will serve as a vital ingredient for completing the local intertwining relation and endoscopic classification for non-quasi-split unitary groups.

papers.title: The Mathieu property for quadratic complements
papers.abstract: For a nondegenerate quadratic form $q$ of dimension $N\geq 1$ over a characteristic-zero field, the kernel of the normalized rotation and scaling trace on $\{q\neq 0\}$ is Mathieu–Zhao exactly when $N\leq 2$. In every higher dimension a single witness attains the minimum pole order, numerator degree and polynomial multiplier degree, namely $(1,3,1)$. A second witness gives sharp degree cutoffs for its detecting multipliers. For an arbitrary regular phase, testing finitely many multipliers at one computable order decides eventual vanishing against every fixed multiplier. For phases affine in the angular variable, a Laurent support criterion suffices. Over $\mathbb{R}$, the kernel of the special orthogonal Reynolds projection is Mathieu–Zhao exactly when $q$ is definite or $N\leq 2$.

papers.title: The Mathieu Property over Fields of Characteristic Zero: Classification and Ground-Field Obstructions
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero and $X$ an affine geometrically homogeneous space of a group $G$ with split reductive identity component. The normalized Reynolds kernel on $K[X]$ is Mathieu–Zhao if and only if $[G^\circ,G^\circ]$ acts trivially. A single active split $\mathrm{SL}_2$ already gives a fixed marked counterexample for a connected reductive acting group. Both results allow $X(K)=\varnothing$. The proof transfers witnesses along principal orbits and specializes marked-moment recurrences over the ground field. We also classify connected reductive groups and compact adjoint semisimple torsors over real closed fields, and representative functions on compact Hausdorff homogeneous spaces. A long-root subgroup gives a further obstruction when a split central torus acts alongside an active compact factor of rank at least two.

papers.title: The Selberg integral at polynomial lengths and pair correlation beyond one
papers.abstract: For every sufficiently large $T$, Montgomery's normalized form factor is at least $0.500001$ throughout $1\le\alpha\le1.0000009$, assuming the Riemann hypothesis for $\zeta$. On a second, wider interval a smaller positive increment also improves the line $3/2-\alpha$. The arithmetic result is unconditional. For $1\le h\le X^{0.001}$, the Selberg integral on $[X,2X]$ exceeds $Xh\{\tfrac12\log(X/h^3)+a\log X\}$ with an absolute $a>0$ for all sufficiently large $X$. We obtain the increment from a second family of Ramanujan sums, supported beyond the square root. The argument also gives the form-factor increment unconditionally for complex differences of zeta zeros.

papers.title: The transverse spin-gradient approximation in noncollinear spin density functional theory
papers.abstract:
We prove a quantitative error bound for a fixed-axis variant of the transverse spin-gradient approximation (TSGA) in noncollinear spin density functional theory. Inspired by Eich and Gross, we use a spin-spiral wave (SSW) as the local reference for the grand-canonical Levy-Lieb energy with the Hartree term subtracted. We construct the thermodynamic limit of the electron gas with constant total density and a prescribed SSW magnetization. Its energy per unit volume $e_{m SSW}$ is evaluated at the local wavevector $
abla\varphi$, where $\varphi$ is the spiral phase. When $\varphi$ is the azimuthal angle of the magnetization $\mathbf{m}=(m_1,m_2,m_3)$, the approximation reads \[ E(ho,\mathbf{m})\approx\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}e_{m SSW} ig(ho(\mathbf{x}),\mathbf{m}(\mathbf{x}),
abla\varphi(\mathbf{x}) ig)\,d \mathbf{x}. \] Here $
abla\varphi$ measures the local rotation of $\mathbf{m}$ about the third axis. Wherever $m_1^2+m_2^2>0$, it equals $(m_1
abla m_2-m_2
abla m_1)/(m_1^2+m_2^2)$. The approximation thus depends only on the total density $ho$, the magnetization and its first derivatives. When the spin-polarized density in the rotating frame and the local wavevector vary on the length scale $N^{1/3}$, with $N$ the mean number of particles, we obtain an error $O(N^{5/6})$ for an energy of order $N$. Setting the phase to zero gives the noncollinear local spin density approximation (LSDA) for arbitrary magnetization directions.

papers.title: Theta Functions and Intrinsic Mirrors of Laurent Phenomenon Algebras
papers.abstract: We construct bases of upper Laurent phenomenon algebras over a field by minimizing Newton polytopes in a single seed. For any translation-invariant total order on the exponents, each least exponent $a$ that occurs determines a smallest Newton polytope $Q_a$. Choose one element with Newton polytope $Q_a$ and least term $x^a$ for each such $a$. These elements form a basis. In every reachable seed chart, every Gauss valuation takes a nonzero basis expansion to the minimum of its values on the nonzero summands. Suppose the algebra has Laurent coefficients and smooth spectrum over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. After setting the curve parameters to one, we compute theta products on the intrinsic mirror from the exchange polynomials and give a finite presentation of the mirror algebra. A seed has a polynomial corner if each exchange polynomial can be multiplied by a unit of the coefficient ring to give a polynomial with constant term one. At such a corner, order the exponents by a weight with strictly positive, rationally independent coordinates. For every lattice exponent $a$ and integral weight $p$, the theta function indexed by $p$ has least $a$-weight $\min_{b\in Q_a}\langle b,p\rangle$ in the corresponding mirror chart. This reciprocity holds for cyclic exchanges and arbitrary pole orders. For fixed exchange supports and constant terms one, we determine when the mirror is smooth and the second mirror recovers the original algebra in the chosen torus coordinates. The coefficient tuples for which both conditions hold form a computable finite set. All their entries are positive integers.

papers.title: Towards a conformal field theory of critical percolation. III. Quantitative mixed fusion and subleading fields
papers.abstract: How does the field produced by closing a small disk arise when two density marks approach each other in critical site percolation on the triangular lattice? We show that the contribution proportional to the scalar field E◦ accumulates over the scales at which the two marked clusters can first merge. After subtracting this logarithmic term from the rescaled, centered density pair, we construct a local field L_ℓ at reference length ℓ. The limit holds in variation norm on the full connectivity record of a surrounding circle, which allows us to derive its conformal transformation law before choosing an exterior observation. We then bring E^◦ or L_r to distance r from a further density mark. After angular averaging and subtraction of the leading density, we obtain expansions with error O(r^(61/40)) at fixed observation radius. The scalar null identity cancels the possible r^(55/48) term for E^◦, leaving r^(3/2)Ψ. For L_r we identify the coefficient of r^(3/2)Ψ and isolate a possible contribution of order r^(55/48). The passage to arbitrary exterior observations uses joint convergence of the connections among interior marks and labelled boundary arcs in the domains left by an exploration.

papers.title: Transcending Algebraic Geometry
papers.abstract: We give an exposition of some of the ideas leading up to Jacob Tsimerman's groundbreaking work developing the theory of o-minimal definability in arithmetic and algebraic geometry.

papers.title: Uniform Algebraic Degeneracy of Entire Curves into Complex Projective Varieties
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to the algebraic degeneracy of entire curves intersecting a simple-normal-crossing divisor on smooth projective varieties over C, within the logarithmic Green-Griffiths-Lang program. For negativelytwisted global logarithmic jet differentials, we introduce an intrinsic weighted conormal filtration along each positive-dimensional closed boundary stratum, with weights prescribed by the contact orders along boundary components. Applying the maximal Harder-Narasimhan slopes of logarithmic cotangent bundles and the normal degrees of the strata, we define an integer vanishing threshold which can improve the pole bound obtained from the slope-based ceiling. Under the stable-base-locus hypothesis for the logarithmic Semple tower, we then establish an improved second main theorem whose counting coefficients depend on the boundary stratum, actual contact orders and the ratio of source weight to twisting exponent. These coefficients are independent of the powers used to realize the stable base locus. We further derive a uniform algebraicdegeneracy criterion allowing positive corrected pole coefficients, formulated via a finite system of stratumwise inequalities together with the ampleness of a residual divisor class. This yields conditional orbifold Green-Griffiths-Lang type statements. Refinements arising from conormalbundle decompositions and sharp local pole estimates at surface boundary crossings are established. Our examples exhibit strict improvement over naive slope-based bounds and illustrate that full-weight poles can persist at boundary crossings, and furnish concrete instances satisfying the stablebaselocus hypothesis.

papers.title: Unimodality of the number of parking functions with a given maximum displacement
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every n, the numbers of parking functions of length n in which the maximum displacement of a car from its preferred spot is 0, 1, . . . , n−1 form a unimodal sequence. This confirms a conjecture of Celano, Elder, Hadaway, Harris, Martin, Priestley and Udell. The proof follows, for each value of the maximum displacement, the sign of the difference of two neighbouring terms as n grows. It is computer-assisted: explicit estimates are used when the displacement is large, and exact computations with integers, carried out by computer, when the displacement or the length is small.

papers.title: Unlikely intersections with CM abelian varieties in a family and explicit bounds for canonical heights under endomorphisms
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{A} \rightarrow S$ be a non-isotrivial abelian scheme over a smooth irreducible curve and let $\mathcal{C} \subseteq \mathcal{A}$ be an irreducible curve, all defined over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$. In 2020, Barroero and Capuano proved that, if $\mathcal{C}$ is not contained in a proper subgroup scheme, then its intersection with the union of the flat subgroup schemes of $\mathcal{A}$ of codimension at least $2$ is finite. We complement this result by proving that, if $\mathcal{C}$ is contained neither in a fixed fiber nor in a proper flat subgroup scheme, even after a finite base change, then only finitely many points of $\mathcal{C}$ lie in a proper algebraic subgroup of a CM fiber of $\mathcal{A}$. This generalizes a previous result of Barroero for fibered powers of elliptic schemes. A key ingredient of the proof is an explicit control of canonical heights under endomorphisms: for an abelian variety $A/\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, an ample symmetric divisor $D$ and $f \in \mathrm{End}(A)$, we bound $\widehat{h}_{A,D}(f(P))$ from above and from below in terms of $\widehat{h}_{A,D}(P)$, with optimal constants given by the largest and the smallest eigenvalue of $f^{\dagger}f$, where $^{\dagger}$ is the Rosati involution associated with $D$.

papers.title: Vanishing results for the coherent cohomology of automorphic vector bundles over the Siegel variety in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: We prove vanishing results for the coherent cohomology of the good reduction modulo $p$ of the Siegel variety with coefficients in some automorphic bundles. We show that for an automorphic bundle with highest weight $\lambda$ near the walls of the anti-dominant Weyl chamber, there is an integer $e \geq 0$ such that the cohomology is concentrated in degrees $[0, e]$. The accessible weights with our method are not necessarily regular and not necessarily $p$-small. Since our method is technical, we also provide an algorithm written in Sage that computes explicitly the vanishing results.

papers.title: Wilson primes for an elliptic coordinate ring of class number one
papers.abstract: Thakur characterised the Wilson primes of F_q[t] (q odd) as the primes with vanishing second derivative, and asked for generalisations to other function fields, for instance of class number one. Let A = F_3[x,y]/(y^2 - x^3 + x + 1), the coordinate ring of an elliptic curve with a single rational point; it is a principal ideal domain. We define a Wilson product W_d in A which reduces to Thakur's F_d in genus 0 and satisfies W_d = -1 mod pi for every prime pi of degree d. We prove that pi is a Wilson prime, i.e. W_d = -1 mod pi^2, if and only if D^2 pi = 0 and the coefficient of the monomial of degree d-1 in pi vanishes, where D is the invariant derivation. The second condition has no counterpart in genus 0. There is no Wilson prime of degree d = 1 mod 3, and y^(4*25^k) + y^(25^k) - 1 (k >= 0) is an infinite family of Wilson primes. The criterion is confirmed by exact computation on all 25430 primes of degree at most 11.

papers.title: Wilson primes for coordinate rings of hyperelliptic curves with one point at infinity
papers.abstract: Let A = F_q[x,y]/(y^2+h(x)y-f(x)) be the coordinate ring of a smooth affine curve of genus g >= 1 with one point at infinity (deg f = 2g+1, deg h <= g), in any characteristic; A need not be principal. With the Wilson product W_d of Hexagon 2611.01007 and 2611.01009, a prime element pi of degree d is called a Wilson prime if W_d = -1 mod pi^2. We prove that W_d = -1 + pi (E(pi) + K_pi D(pi)) / D(pi)^2 mod pi^2, so that pi is a Wilson prime if and only if pi divides E(pi) + K_pi D(pi), where D is the invariant derivation, E = (h^2+4f) d_x^(2) + (f' + h'(y+h)) d_x is a second order operator written with Hasse derivatives, the same in every characteristic, and K_pi is defined by a canonical decomposition; for d >= 2g it is a polynomial in x of degree less than g, given by an explicit recipe in terms of the leading coefficients of pi. This contains the divisibility criteria of the two earlier notes for the four rings of class number one, and Thakur's criterion for F_q[t] has the same shape. The statement is confirmed by exact computation on 17 curves of genus 1, 2, 3 in characteristics 2, 3, 5, 7.

papers.title: Wilson primes for coordinate rings of plane curves with one point at infinity
papers.abstract: Let A = F_q[x,y]/(F) be the coordinate ring of a smooth affine plane curve F = y^a - alpha x^b + lower terms with gcd(a,b) = 1; such a curve has one point at infinity. With the Wilson product W_d attached to the monomial basis, we prove for every prime element pi of degree d the congruence W_d = -1 + pi (E(pi) + K_pi D pi)/(D pi)^2 mod pi^2, where D is the invariant derivation, E an explicit second order operator and K_pi a correction term defined by a canonical decomposition involving at most g monomials. This extends to all these curves the theorem proved for hyperelliptic curves in Hexagon 2611.01011. For the curves y^a = f(x) and the prime elements P(y) the correction vanishes; when f' is a non-zero constant and the second Hasse derivative of f is zero, P(y) is a Wilson prime if and only if the second Hasse derivative of P is zero, which is Thakur's criterion for F_q[t] with y in the role of t. We deduce infinitely many Wilson primes on y^a = x^p - x + alpha over F_p for every odd p and every a >= 2 prime to p, and on y^a = x^4 + x + 1 over F_2 for every odd a >= 3.

papers.title: Wilson primes for the coordinate rings of class number one in characteristic two
papers.abstract: Besides the polynomial rings, four coordinate rings A of a curve over a finite field minus one rational point have class number one. For the one of characteristic 3, the Wilson primes were characterised in Hexagon 2611.01007. We treat the three rings of characteristic 2: y^2+y=x^3+x+1 over F_2, y^2+y=x^3+alpha over F_4, and y^2+y=x^5+x^3+1 over F_2 (genus 2). A prime pi of degree d is a Wilson prime, i.e. W_d = -1 mod pi^2, if and only if pi divides D2(pi) + (f' + kappa) D(pi), where D = d/dx, D2 is the second Hasse derivative and kappa is an explicit function of the leading coefficients of pi. In genus 1 this is equivalent to D2(pi) = t D(t pi) with t = x + a, a explicit, and there is no Wilson prime of degree 0 or 3 mod 4. In genus 2 it is equivalent to D2(pi) + (x^4+x^2+kappa) D(pi) = (x^2+x+1+kappa) pi for d >= 4, and there is no Wilson prime of degree 2 or 3 mod 4, d >= 4. The criteria are confirmed by exact computation on 15302 primes. The product W_d refers to the given model of the ring.

papers.title: « Le triangulaire d'un carré » : une note inédite attribuée à Sophie Germain (BnF, NAF 4073)
papers.abstract: Volume NAF 4073 of the Bibliothèque nationale de France gathers letters to and from Sophie Germain. On the verso of folio 32, the cover of an unsigned letter of 13 March 1814, a note in a hand other than the letter's states that "the triangular number of a square is the sum of the squares of the two consecutive triangular numbers", and writes ((n²−n)/2)² + ((n²+n)/2)² = (n⁴+n²)/2. It is the only line of mathematics in the volume, and neither the catalogues nor the studies consulted mention it. It is in Germain's hand: the manuscript dated "circa 1797" by the bookseller Quaritch and reproduced by Alexanderson gives the same identity in the same notation, after "J'ai aussi remarqué que", and writes in symbols what the sentence of NAF 4073 says in words. The identity was known; the note was not. A last section extends Germain's computation to power sums expressed in terms of T_n; every statement is proved in Lean 4.
